Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 8, verses 1–2:

Many exegetes (mufassirun) explicitly stated that it is Madani and did not exclude any part of it from that. This was the view of al-Hasan, ʿIkrima, Jabir ibn Zayd and ʿAta'.

Something similar has been related from Ibn ʿAbbas. Al-Nahhas related it in his book on abrogation (Nasikh) and Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh (transmitted it) from him, who said: "Surat al-Anfal was revealed in Medina."

Ibn Mardawayh also related it from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr.

Ibn Mardawayh also related it from Zayd ibn Thabit.

Sa'id ibn Mansur, al-Bukhari, Ibn al-Mundhir, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: "It was revealed concerning Badr." In another wording: "That is the surah of Badr."

Al-Qurtubi said: "Ibn ʿAbbas said: 'It is Madani except for seven verses from His saying: ﴿And [remember] when those who disbelieved plotted against you﴾ (al-Anfal: 30–36), up to the end of the seven verses. The total number of verses of this surah is seventy-six. The Prophet (ﷺ) used to recite it in the Maghrib prayer.'" Al-Tabarani related it with a sound chain from Abu Ayyub, as did Zayd ibn Thabit: "from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he used to recite Surat al-Anfal in the two rak'ahs of the Maghrib prayer."

* *

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Al-Anfal is the plural of nafl (a gift or extra portion), with a vowel on the first letter, and it means spoils of war (ghanima). From it is the saying of ʿAntara:

"When the battle reddens, we quench our spears, and we abstain at the division of the spoils (al-anfal)."

That is, the spoils of war. The root meaning of nafl is increase or addition. The spoils are called by this name because they are an addition to what Allah made lawful for this Ummah which had been forbidden to others, or because they are an addition to the reward that the fighter (mujahid) obtains from jihad. The word nafl is also used with other meanings, among them oath, seeking, and a well-known plant.

Al-nafila means voluntary worship (tatawwuʿ), because it is an addition to what is obligatory. Al-nafila also means a grandson (son's son), because he is an addition to the son.

The occasion of revelation of the verse was the disagreement of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, on the day of Badr, as will be explained. So Allah took away from their hands what they had gained and made it for Allah and the Messenger. He said: ﴿Say: The spoils belong to Allah and the Messenger﴾. That is: the ruling concerning them belongs exclusively to the two of them. The Messenger of Allah divides them among you by the command of Allah, the Exalted, and you have no say in that.

A group of the Companions and the Successors (tabiʿun) held that the spoils were exclusively for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and that no one else had any share in them, until He revealed His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And know that whatever you obtain as spoils, then for Allah is one-fifth of it﴾ (al-Anfal: 41).

Then He commanded them to have taqwa (God-consciousness), to reconcile among themselves, and to obey Allah and His Messenger by submitting to their command, and to abandon the disagreement that had occurred among them. Then He said: ﴿if you are believers﴾, that is: carry out these three commands if you are believers in Allah. In this there is an incitement and stirring up that is not hidden, even though they were in that state upon faith. It is as if He said: "If you are steadfast upon faith in Allah," because these three matters, which are God-consciousness, reconciliation among people, and obedience to Allah and His Messenger, faith is not complete without them. Rather, faith is not established at all for one who does not carry them out, for whoever is not God-conscious and does not obey Allah and His Messenger is not a believer.

Ahmad, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan related from Abu Umama who said: "I asked ʿUbada ibn al-Samit about al-Anfal, and he said: 'It was revealed about us, the companions of Badr, when we disagreed over the nafl and our characters deteriorated because of it. So Allah took it from our hands and made it for the Messenger (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah divided it among the Muslims equally (ʿan bawaʾ), (that is) on an equal basis (ʿan sawaʾ).'"

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ahmad, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, al-Hakim (who declared it sound), Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan related from ʿUbada ibn al-Samit who said: "We went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and I witnessed Badr with him. The people met, and Allah defeated the enemy. A group pursued them, routing and killing them. Another group stooped over the camp, seizing and gathering it. And a group surrounded the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so that the enemy could not catch him unawares. When night came and the people returned to one another, those who had gathered the spoils said: 'We gathered them and collected them, so no one has a share in them.' (p-524) Those who had gone out in pursuit of the enemy said: 'You are not more entitled to them than us. We repelled the enemy from him and defeated them.' And those who had surrounded the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'You are not more entitled to them than us. We surrounded the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and feared that the enemy would catch him unawares, so we busied ourselves with him.' Then the revelation came: ﴿They ask you about the spoils. Say: The spoils belong to Allah and the Messenger﴾. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) divided them among the Muslims. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) raided into enemy territory, he would give a quarter as nafl, and when he returned and the people were all gathered, he would give a third as nafl. He disliked the nafl and would say: 'Let the strong among the Muslims return to their weak.'"

Ishaq ibn Rahawayh in his Musnad, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh related from Abu Ayyub al-Ansari who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent a sariyya (raiding detachment). Allah gave it victory and conquest over them. Whoever brought him something, he gave him a nafl from the khums (one-fifth). Some men who had been advancing, killing and capturing returned, and they had left the spoils behind them, so they obtained none of the spoils. They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what is the matter with men of ours who advance and take captives, while men who stayed behind and did not join the fighting are given a share of the spoils?' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained silent, and the revelation came: ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾ (the verse). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called them and said: 'Return what you have taken and divide it with justice and equality, for Allah commands you to do so.' They said: 'We have spent it and eaten it.' He said: 'Count that as a reward (ihtisab).'"

Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi (who declared it sound), al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Nuʿaym in al-Hilya, al-Hakim (who declared it sound), Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan related "from Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas who said: 'I said: O Messenger of Allah, Allah has relieved me today of the polytheists, so give me this sword.' He said: 'This sword is neither yours nor mine. Put it down.' So I put it down. Then I returned and said: 'Perhaps this sword will be given today to someone who has not shown the trials I have shown.' Then a man called to me from behind: 'I said: Has Allah revealed something concerning me?' He said: 'You asked me for this sword, and it was not mine. Now it has been given to me, so it is yours.' And Allah revealed this verse: ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾." In another wording of Ahmad: "Saʿd said: 'When my brother was killed on the day of Badr and I killed Saʿid ibn al-ʿAs and took his sword, which was called Dhu al-Kanifa, I brought it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).'" Then he mentioned something similar to what preceded. This hadith has been related from Saʿd through other routes.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh related from ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from his father, from his grandfather: "The people asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the spoils on the day of Badr, and the revelation came: ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾."

Ibn Mardawayh also related from him (ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb?) who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) did not give any nafl after the revelation of ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾ except from the khums, for he gave a nafl from the khums on the day of Khaybar."

Ibn Abi Shayba, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Hibban, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Hakim (who declared it sound), Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il related from Ibn ʿAbbas who said: "On the day of Badr the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Whoever kills a slain enemy, for him is such-and-such, and whoever takes a captive, for him is such-and-such.' As for the elders (mashyakha), they stood firm beneath the banners, but the young men hastened to the killing and the spoils. The elders said to the young men: 'Share them with us, for we were a support for you. Had there been any danger for you, you would have taken refuge with us.' So they disputed before the Prophet (ﷺ), and the revelation came: ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾ (the verse). Then the Prophet (ﷺ) divided the spoils among them equally."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan related from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying: ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾, he said: "al-Anfal are the spoils (maghanim). They belonged exclusively to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and no one had any share in them, whatever the detachments (sara ya) of the Muslims obtained and brought to him. Whoever withheld from it a needle or a thread, that is ghulul (embezzlement). They asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to give them some of it, so Allah revealed: ﴿They ask you about the spoils. Say: The spoils belong to Allah and the Messenger﴾, that is, I have made them and My Messenger's, and you have no share in them, ﴿so fear Allah and set right the state of your affairs﴾ up to His saying: ﴿if you are believers﴾. Then Allah revealed: ﴿And know that whatever you obtain as spoils﴾ (al-Anfal: 41), the verse. Then He divided that one-fifth for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), for the near kin, the orphans, the needy, and the emigrants in the way of Allah. He made the four-fifths for the people equal in it: for the horse two shares, for its rider one share, and for the foot soldier one share."

Abu ʿUbayd and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾, that he said: "They are the spoils, and then it (the ruling) was abrogated (nasakha) by ﴿And know that whatever you obtain as spoils﴾, the verse."

Malik, Ibn Abi Shayba, Abu ʿUbayd, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Nahhas, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh related from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad who said: "I heard a man ask Ibn ʿAbbas about al-Anfal, and he said: 'The horse is from the nafl, and the spoils of the slain (salab) are from the nafl.' He repeated the question, and Ibn ʿAbbas said: 'This is like Dhubay' whom ʿUmar struck.'" In another wording: "He said: 'How much you need to be dealt with as ʿUmar dealt with Dhubay' al-ʿIraqi,' and ʿUmar had struck him until the blood flowed down his heels."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from him (Ibn ʿAbbas) who said: "al-Anfal are the spoils. They were commanded to reconcile among themselves concerning them, so that the strong would return them to the weak."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Nahhas and Abu al-Shaykh related from ʿAta' concerning His saying: ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾, he said: "It is what strayed from the polytheists to the Muslims without fighting, whether a slave, an animal or goods. That belongs to the Prophet (ﷺ), who does with it whatever he wishes."

Ibn Abi Shayba, Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh related from Muhammad ibn ʿAmr who said: "We sent to Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab to ask him about al-Anfal, and he said: 'You ask me about al-Anfal, and there is no nafl after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).'"

ʿAbd al-Razzaq related from Saʿid as well, who said: "They did not give nafl except from the khums." And ʿAbd al-Razzaq related from him that he said: "There is no nafl in the spoils of the Muslims except in the khums of the khums."

ʿAbd al-Razzaq related from Anas that a commander wanted to give him a nafl before the khums was taken out of it, but Anas refused to accept it until it had been taken out as khums.

Ibn Abi Shayba, ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Shaʿbi, concerning His saying: ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾, he said: "They are what the detachments obtained."

Ibn Abi Shayba, Ibn Jarir and al-Nahhas in his book on abrogation related from Mujahid and ʿIkrima who said: "The spoils belonged to Allah and the Messenger until the verse of the khums abrogated it: ﴿And know that whatever you obtain as spoils﴾ (al-Anfal: 41), the verse."

Ibn Abi Shayba, al-Bukhari in al-Adab al-Mufrad, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in Shuʿab al-Iman related from (p-525) Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying: ﴿and set right the state of your affairs﴾, he said: "This is an admonition from Allah to the believers that they should fear Allah and reconcile among themselves, since they disagreed about the spoils."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Makhul who said: "The reconciliation among them was that the spoils were returned and then divided between those who stood firm with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and those who fought and gained spoils."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from ʿAta' concerning His saying: ﴿and obey Allah and His Messenger﴾, he said: "Obedience to the Messenger is following the Book and the Sunna."

Ibn Abi Shayba, Ibn Jarir and al-Nahhas in his book on abrogation related from Mujahid and ʿIkrima who said: "The spoils belonged to Allah and the Messenger until the verse of the khums abrogated it: ﴿And know that whatever you obtain as spoils﴾ (al-Anfal: 41), the verse."

Ibn Abi Shayba, al-Bukhari in al-Adab al-Mufrad, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in Shuʿab al-Iman related from (p-525) Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying: ﴿and set right the state of your affairs﴾, he said: "This is an admonition from Allah to the believers that they should fear Allah and reconcile among themselves, since they disagreed about the spoils."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Makhul who said: "The reconciliation among them was that the spoils were returned and then divided between those who stood firm with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and those who fought and gained spoils."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from ʿAta' concerning His saying: ﴿and obey Allah and His Messenger﴾, he said: "Obedience to the Messenger is following the Book and the Sunna."

Al-Shawkani, *Fath al-Qadir*, commentary on Surah 8, verses 3–4:

Al-wajal means fear and dread. The intended meaning is that the arising of fear of God and dread of Him when He is mentioned is the condition of the believers who have complete faith and are sincere to God. The restriction here is made in terms of the perfection of faith, not in terms of its basic essence.

A group of the commentators (*mufassirun*) said: this verse includes an exhortation to obey the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in what he commanded regarding the division of the spoils of war. You are not unaware that, although it is valid to include this within the meaning of the verse, since the trembling of hearts at the remembrance (of God) and the increase of faith upon the recitation of God's verses necessarily entail carrying out what He, glory be to Him, commanded regarding the spoils being for God and the Messenger, nevertheless the apparent purpose of the verse is to establish this quality for those whose faith is complete, without restricting it to one state rather than another, nor to one time rather than another, nor to one event rather than another. By the recitation of His verses is meant the recitation of the revealed verses, or the expression of His wondrous craftsmanship and the perfection of His power in His created signs, by mentioning their wondrous creation and their marvels, at the mention of which the believers humble themselves.

It has been said: by the increase of faith is meant an increase in the expansion of the breast, the tranquility of the heart, and the serenity of the mind upon the recitation of the verses. It has also been said: by the increase of faith is meant an increase in action, because faith is one thing that neither increases nor decreases. The numerous verses and the mutawatir (widely transmitted) hadiths refute and reject this view.

﴿وَعَلَىٰ رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ﴾ (and upon their Lord they rely), not upon anyone else. Tawakkul (reliance upon God) is the entrusting of all affairs to Him.

The relative pronoun in His saying ﴿الَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ الصَّلَاةَ﴾ (those who establish the prayer) is in the nominative case, either as a description of the relative pronoun before it, or as a substitute for it, or as an explanation of it. It may also be in the accusative case, by way of praise. He singled out the establishment of prayer and the giving of charity because these two are the root and foundation of good. The *min* in *mimma* (from what) is partitive. The reference in His saying ﴿أُولَٰئِكَ﴾ (those) is to the people characterized by the attributes mentioned earlier. It is the subject, and its predicate is ﴿هُمُ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ (they are the believers), meaning that these are the ones of complete faith, who have reached its highest levels and its furthest goals. The word *haqqan* (truly) is an emphatic infinitive confirming the content of the sentence ﴿هُمُ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ﴾, meaning: that is true, a true confirmation; or it is an adjective of an omitted infinitive, meaning: they are believers in true faith.

Then He mentioned what He has prepared for those who combine these attributes of honor, saying: ﴿لَهُمْ دَرَجَاتٌ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ وَمَغْفِرَةٌ وَرِزْقٌ كَرِيمٌ﴾ (For them are ranks with their Lord, and forgiveness and generous provision). Darajat means stations of goodness, honor, and nobility in Paradise. Their being with Him, glory be to Him, is an increase in their ennoblement, honoring, exaltation, and magnification. The clause ﴿لَهُمْ دَرَجَاتٌ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ is either a second predicate of ﴿أُولَٰئِكَ﴾, or a resumptive sentence answering an implied question. *Maghfira* (forgiveness) is coordinated with *darajat*, meaning: forgiveness for their sins, and generous provision which God bestows upon them from His vast favor and overflowing bounty.

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿وَجِلَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾ (their hearts tremble), that he said: their hearts are frightened.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also reported from him regarding the verse: the hypocrites, nothing of the remembrance of God enters their hearts when fulfilling His obligations, they do not believe in any of God's signs, they do not rely upon God, they do not maintain family ties when they are absent, and they do not pay the zakat on their wealth. So God informed that they are not believers. Then He described the believers, saying: ﴿إِنَّمَا الْمُؤْمِنُونَ الَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِرَ اللَّهُ وَجِلَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾ (The believers are only those who, when God is mentioned, their hearts tremble), and so they fulfill His obligations.

Al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, and Abu al-Shaykh reported through the route of Shahr ibn Hawshab from Umm al-Darda', who said: indeed the trembling in the heart is like the burning of a palm frond. O Shahr ibn Hawshab, do you not feel a shiver? I said: yes. She said: then supplicate at that moment, for supplication is answered at that time.

Al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi reported from Thabit al-Bunani, who said: a certain man said: I know when my supplication will be answered. They said: how do you know that? He said: when my skin shivers, my heart trembles, and my eyes overflow, that is the moment my supplication is answered.

He also reported from Aisha, who said: the trembling in the heart of the believer is nothing but like the kindling of a palm frond. So when one of you trembles, let him supplicate at that moment.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh reported from al-Suddi regarding the verse that he said: it is the man who intends to wrong someone or is about to commit an act of disobedience, and it is said to him: fear God, and his heart trembles.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh reported from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying ﴿زَادَتْهُمْ إِيمَانًا﴾ (it increases them in faith) that he said: (it means) affirmation (*tasdiq*).

These same reported from al-Rabi' ibn Anas regarding His saying ﴿زَادَتْهُمْ إِيمَانًا﴾ that he said: (it means) fear (*khashya*).

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying ﴿وَعَلَىٰ رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ﴾ that he said: they hope for none other than Him.

Both of them also reported from him regarding His saying ﴿أُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ حَقًّا﴾ (those are truly the believers) that he said: they are free of disbelief.

Abu al-Shaykh reported from him regarding *haqqan* (truly) that he said: pure, sincere.

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding His saying ﴿لَهُمْ دَرَجَاتٌ﴾ that he meant virtues and mercy.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh reported from Mujahid regarding His saying ﴿لَهُمْ دَرَجَاتٌ﴾ that he said: they are elevated deeds.

Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from al-Dahhak regarding His saying ﴿لَهُمْ دَرَجَاتٌ﴾ that he said: the people of Paradise are above one another in rank, so the one who is above sees his superiority over the one who is below him, while the one who is below does not see that anyone has been preferred over him.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh reported from Ibn Zayd regarding His saying ﴿وَمَغْفِرَةٌ﴾ that he said: (it means) by leaving off sins, and ﴿وَرِزْقٌ كَرِيمٌ﴾ he said: righteous deeds.

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who said: whenever you hear God say ﴿وَرِزْقٌ كَرِيمٌ﴾, it is Paradise.

**Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on Surah 8, verses 5–8:**

[p. 526] His saying: ﴿As your Lord brought you out of your house in truth﴾.

Al-Zajjaj (al-Zajjaj, grammarian) said: the *kaf* (the "as" particle) is in the accusative position, meaning: the spoils are established for you just as your Lord brought you out of your house in truth, that is, like the bringing out by your Lord. The meaning is: proceed in accordance with His command concerning the spoils, and grant extra shares to whomever you wish, even if they dislike it. This is because some of the Companions said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when it was decreed that each person who brought a captive would receive something: "Most people have been left with nothing." So the position of the *kaf* is accusative, as we have mentioned. Al-Farra' (al-Farra', grammarian) also said this.

Abu 'Ubayda (Abu 'Ubayda, philologist) said: it is an oath, meaning "by the One who brought you out," so the *kaf* has the sense of the *waw* (of swearing), and *ma* has the sense of *alladhi* (who).

Al-Akhfash Sa'id ibn Mas'ada (al-Akhfash, grammarian) said: the meaning is, "Those are the true believers, just as your Lord brought you out."

'Ikrima (Ikrima, a Successor) said the meaning is: obey Allah and His Messenger, just as your Lord brought you out.

It was also said that "as He brought you out" is connected to His saying ﴿they will have ranks﴾, meaning: this promise to the believers is true in the Hereafter, ﴿just as your Lord brought you out of your house in truth﴾, which is due to Him. So He fulfilled your promise, granted you victory over your enemy, and gave you what was due. This was mentioned and preferred by al-Nahhas (al-Nahhas, grammarian).

It was also said that the *kaf* in "kama" is the *kaf* of comparison in the manner of recompense, like the saying of a person to his servant: "Just as I directed you against my enemies, and they overcame you, and you asked for reinforcement so I reinforced you and strengthened you and removed your weakness, so now seize them and punish them."

It was also said that the *kaf* is in the nominative position, as the predicate of an omitted subject, its estimated form being: "This state is like the state of your bringing out," meaning that their dislike of what you saw of distributing the spoils to the fighters is like their dislike of your going out to war. This was mentioned by the author of al-Kashshaf (al-Zamakhshari, author of al-Kashshaf). "In truth" is connected to an omitted element, and the estimate is: a bringing out accompanied by the truth which has no doubt in it.

The clause ﴿and indeed a group of the believers were averse﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (*hal*): that is, as He brought you out while they were averse to it. This is because when Allah promised them one of the two groups, either the caravan or the army, they desired the caravan because of the booty it contained and because it was safe from fighting, as will be explained later.

The clause ﴿they argue with you concerning the truth after it has become clear﴾ is either in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause following another circumstantial clause, or it is a new clause answering an implied question. Their argument concerned His commanding them to face one of the two groups; the caravan had escaped, and He commanded them to fight the army, while they did not have great readiness with them. Therefore it was hard for them, and they said: "If you had told us about the fighting, we would have taken equipment and completed our preparation." The meaning of "concerning the truth" is: concerning the fighting, after it had become clear to them that you do not command anything except by the permission of Allah, or after it had become clear to them that Allah had promised them victory over one of the two groups, and that if the caravan escaped, they would gain victory over the army. "After" is an adverbial of time governing "they argue with you," and *ma* is a verbal (infinitival) particle, meaning: they argue with you after the truth has become clear to them.

His saying: ﴿as if they were being driven toward death while they looked on﴾. The *kaf* is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause relating to the pronoun in "averse," meaning: in the state of their extreme terror of fighting, they resemble one who is being driven to be killed while he is watching the causes of his killing, looking at them, not doubting them.

His saying: ﴿And when Allah promised you one of the two groups, that it would be yours﴾. The adverbial phrase is in the accusative position governed by an omitted verb, meaning: remember the time when Allah promised you one of the two groups. He commanded them to remember the time, though the intention is to mention the events that occurred in it, for the sake of emphasis. The two groups are the caravan and the army. "One" is the second object of "promised," and "that it would be yours" is a substitute for it, a substitute of inclusion. Its meaning is: that it is subjected to you, that you will overcome it, take booty from it, and do with it what you wish of killing, capture, and plunder; they cannot repel you, and they cannot control for themselves any harm or benefit from you. In this clause there is a reminder to them of one of the blessings with which Allah favored them.

His saying: ﴿and you wished﴾ is conjoined to "He promises you," among the events whose times they were commanded to remember: that the group without the thorn (armed strength), which is the caravan group, would be yours rather than the group with the thorn, which is the army.

Abu 'Ubayda said: that is, the group without the edge.

*Al-shawka* means weapons, and *al-shawka* also means a plant that has a point, from which comes the phrase "a man sharp of weapons," meaning sharp-edged in weapons, then it is inverted to say "sharp of weapons." So *al-shawka* is used metaphorically from the single thorn. The meaning is: you wished to overcome the group that had no weapons, which is the caravan group, because it would be pure booty free from the turmoil of fighting, since there was no one with it to defend it.

His saying: ﴿and Allah wills to establish the truth by His words﴾ is conjoined to "you wished," and it is among the events whose times they were commanded to remember. That is: Allah wills something other than what you wish, namely to establish the truth by manifesting it, in accordance with what He decreed of your victory over the group with strength, their killing of their chieftains, the capture of many of them, and your seizing of the wealth they had brought against you, with which they sought to repel you. "The words" refer to the verses He revealed concerning fighting the group with strength, and His promise to them of victory over it. ﴿And cut off the last remnant of the disbelievers﴾: *dābir* is the last, and cutting it off is an expression for uprooting, meaning: He will entirely eradicate them.

His saying: ﴿so that He might establish the truth and nullify falsehood﴾. This clause is the reason for what Allah wills: that is, He willed that, or He wills that, in order to manifest the truth and raise it, and to nullify falsehood and abase it. Or the *lam* is connected to an omitted element: that is, He did that so that He might establish the truth. It was also said that it is connected to "He cuts off." This clause is not a repetition of what came before it, because the first clause explains the difference between the two wills, while this clause explains the wisdom that calls for it, the reason that requires it, and the benefit that results from it. "Establishing the truth" is making it manifest, and "nullifying falsehood" is annihilating it. ﴿Rather, We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it crushes it, and behold, it vanishes﴾ (al-Anbiya': 18). The object of ﴿though the criminals dislike it﴾ is omitted, meaning: though they dislike that He should establish the truth and nullify falsehood. The criminals are the polytheists of Quraysh, or all groups of disbelievers.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il (Dala'il al-Nubuwwa) have narrated from Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us while we were in Medina, and news had reached him that the caravan of Abu Sufyan had approached. He said: 'What do you think about it? Perhaps Allah will give it to us as booty and grant us safety.' So we set out. When we had travelled a day or two, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to count ourselves, and we did so, and we were three hundred and thirteen. We informed the Prophet ﷺ of our number, and he rejoiced at that and praised Allah and said: 'The number of the companions of Talut.' Then he said: 'What do you think about fighting the people? They have been informed of your departure.' We said: 'O Messenger of Allah, no, by Allah, we have no strength to fight the people; we only went out for the caravan.' Then he said: 'What do you think about fighting the people?' We said the same as before. Al-Miqdad said: 'Do not say as the people of Moses said to Moses: "So go, you and your Lord, and fight; indeed, we are sitting here" (al-Ma'ida: 24).' Then Allah revealed: ﴿As your Lord brought you out﴾ up to His saying: ﴿and when Allah promised you one of the two groups, that it would be yours﴾. When Allah promised us one of the two groups, either the people or the caravan, our hearts were content. Then we met the people, and we lined up. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'O Allah, I ask You to fulfill Your promise.' Then Ibn Rawaha said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I wish to advise you, though the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is too excellent to be advised. Indeed Allah is greater and more majestic than that you should ask Him to fulfill His promise.' He said: 'O son of Rawaha, I will indeed ask Allah to fulfill His promise, for Allah does not break His promise.' Then he took a handful of dust and threw it at the faces of the people, and they fled. Then Allah revealed: ﴿And you did not throw when you threw, but Allah threw﴾ (al-Anfal: 17). So we killed and captured. Then 'Umar said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I do not think you should have captives, for we are only to call and conciliate.' We said: 'O assembly of the Ansar, 'Umar says what he says only out of envy toward us.' Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ slept, then awoke and said: 'Call 'Umar to me.' He was called, and he said: 'Indeed Allah has revealed to me: ﴿It is not for a prophet to have captives﴾ (al-Anfal: 67), the verse.'" In its chain is Ibn Lahi'a, and concerning him there is a well-known discussion.

**Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on Surah 8, verses 5–8:**

[p. 526] His saying: ﴿As your Lord brought you out of your house in truth﴾.

The meaning is: proceed in accordance with His command concerning the spoils, and grant extra shares to whomever you wish, even if they dislike it. This is because some of the Companions said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when it was decreed that each person who brought a captive would receive something: "Most people have been left with nothing." So the position of the *kaf* is accusative, as we have mentioned. Al-Farra' (al-Farra', grammarian) also said this.

Abu 'Ubayda (Abu 'Ubayda, philologist) said: it is an oath, meaning "by the One who brought you out," so the *kaf* has the sense of the *waw* (of swearing), and *ma* has the sense of *alladhi* (who).

Al-Akhfash Sa'id ibn Mas'ada (al-Akhfash, grammarian) said: the meaning is, "Those are the true believers, just as your Lord brought you out."

'Ikrima (Ikrima, a Successor) said the meaning is: obey Allah and His Messenger, just as your Lord brought you out.

It was also said that "as He brought you out" is connected to His saying ﴿they will have ranks﴾, meaning: this promise to the believers is true in the Hereafter, ﴿just as your Lord brought you out of your house in truth﴾, which is due to Him. So He fulfilled your promise, granted you victory over your enemy, and gave you what was due. This was mentioned and preferred by al-Nahhas (al-Nahhas, grammarian).

It was also said that the *kaf* in "kama" is the *kaf* of comparison in the manner of recompense, like the saying of a person to his servant: "Just as I directed you against my enemies, and they overcame you, and you asked for reinforcement so I reinforced you and strengthened you and removed your weakness, so now seize them and punish them."

It was also said that the *kaf* is in the nominative position, as the predicate of an omitted subject, its estimated form being: "This state is like the state of your bringing out," meaning that their dislike of what you saw of distributing the spoils to the fighters is like their dislike of your going out to war. This was mentioned by the author of al-Kashshaf (al-Zamakhshari, author of al-Kashshaf). "In truth" is connected to an omitted element, and the estimate is: a bringing out accompanied by the truth which has no doubt in it.

The clause ﴿and indeed a group of the believers were averse﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (*hal*): that is, as He brought you out while they were averse to it. This is because when Allah promised them one of the two groups, either the caravan or the army, they desired the caravan because of the booty it contained and because it was safe from fighting, as will be explained later.

The clause ﴿they argue with you concerning the truth after it has become clear﴾ is either in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause following another circumstantial clause, or it is a new clause answering an implied question. Their argument concerned His commanding them to face one of the two groups; the caravan had escaped, and He commanded them to fight the army, while they did not have great readiness with them. Therefore it was hard for them, and they said: "If you had told us about the fighting, we would have taken equipment and completed our preparation." The meaning of "concerning the truth" is: concerning the fighting, after it had become clear to them that you do not command anything except by the permission of Allah, or after it had become clear to them that Allah had promised them victory over one of the two groups, and that if the caravan escaped, they would gain victory over the army. "After" is an adverbial of time governing "they argue with you," and *ma* is a verbal (infinitival) particle, meaning: they argue with you after the truth has become clear to them.

His saying: ﴿as if they were being driven toward death while they looked on﴾. The *kaf* is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause relating to the pronoun in "averse," meaning: in the state of their extreme terror of fighting, they resemble one who is being driven to be killed while he is watching the causes of his killing, looking at them, not doubting them.

His saying: ﴿And when Allah promised you one of the two groups, that it would be yours﴾. The adverbial phrase is in the accusative position governed by an omitted verb, meaning: remember the time when Allah promised you one of the two groups. He commanded them to remember the time, though the intention is to mention the events that occurred in it, for the sake of emphasis. The two groups are the caravan and the army. "One" is the second object of "promised," and "that it would be yours" is a substitute for it, a substitute of inclusion. Its meaning is: that it is subjected to you, that you will overcome it, take booty from it, and do with it what you wish of killing, capture, and plunder; they cannot repel you, and they cannot control for themselves any harm or benefit from you. In this clause there is a reminder to them of one of the blessings with which Allah favored them.

His saying: ﴿and you wished﴾ is conjoined to "He promises you," among the events whose times they were commanded to remember: that the group without the thorn (armed strength), which is the caravan group, would be yours rather than the group with the thorn, which is the army.

Abu 'Ubayda said: that is, the group without the edge.

*Al-shawka* means weapons, and *al-shawka* also means a plant that has a point, from which comes the phrase "a man sharp of weapons," meaning sharp-edged in weapons, then it is inverted to say "sharp of weapons." So *al-shawka* is used metaphorically from the single thorn. The meaning is: you wished to overcome the group that had no weapons, which is the caravan group, because it would be pure booty free from the turmoil of fighting, since there was no one with it to defend it.

His saying: ﴿and Allah wills to establish the truth by His words﴾ is conjoined to "you wished," and it is among the events whose times they were commanded to remember. That is: Allah wills something other than what you wish, namely to establish the truth by manifesting it, in accordance with what He decreed of your victory over the group with strength, their killing of their chieftains, the capture of many of them, and your seizing of the wealth they had brought against you, with which they sought to repel you. "The words" refer to the verses He revealed concerning fighting the group with strength, and His promise to them of victory over it. ﴿And cut off the last remnant of the disbelievers﴾: *dābir* is the last, and cutting it off is an expression for uprooting, meaning: He will entirely eradicate them.

His saying: ﴿so that He might establish the truth and nullify falsehood﴾. This clause is the reason for what Allah wills: that is, He willed that, or He wills that, in order to manifest the truth and raise it, and to nullify falsehood and abase it. This clause is not a repetition of what came before it, because the first clause explains the difference between the two wills, while this clause explains the wisdom that calls for it, the reason that requires it, and the benefit that results from it. "Establishing the truth" is making it manifest, and "nullifying falsehood" is annihilating it. ﴿Rather, We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it crushes it, and behold, it vanishes﴾ (al-Anbiya': 18). Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from al-Dahhak concerning His saying: ﴿and you wished that the group without the thorn would be yours﴾: "It is the caravan of Abu Sufyan. The companions of Muhammad ﷺ wished that the caravan would be theirs and that the fighting would be diverted from them."

'Abd ibn Humayd narrated from Qatada concerning ﴿and cut off the last remnant of the disbelievers﴾: "that is, their root."

The battle of Badr has been comprehensively recorded in the books of hadith, biography, and history, so we will not lengthen it by mentioning it here.

**Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on Surah 8, verses 5–8:**

[p. 526] His saying: ﴿As your Lord brought you out of your house in truth﴾.

Al-Zajjaj (al-Zajjaj, grammarian) said: the *kaf* (the "as" particle) is in the accusative position, meaning: the spoils are established for you just as your Lord brought you out of your house in truth, that is, like the bringing out by your Lord. The meaning is: proceed in accordance with His command concerning the spoils, and grant extra shares to whomever you wish, even if they dislike it. This is because some of the Companions said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when it was decreed that each person who brought a captive would receive something: "Most people have been left with nothing." So the position of the *kaf* is accusative, as we have mentioned. Al-Farra' (al-Farra', grammarian) also said this.

Abu 'Ubayda (Abu 'Ubayda, philologist) said: it is an oath, meaning "by the One who brought you out," so the *kaf* has the sense of the *waw* (of swearing), and *ma* has the sense of *alladhi* (who).

Al-Akhfash Sa'id ibn Mas'ada (al-Akhfash, grammarian) said: the meaning is, "Those are the true believers, just as your Lord brought you out."

'Ikrima (Ikrima, a Successor) said the meaning is: obey Allah and His Messenger, just as your Lord brought you out.

It was also said that "as He brought you out" is connected to His saying ﴿they will have ranks﴾, meaning: this promise to the believers is true in the Hereafter, ﴿just as your Lord brought you out of your house in truth﴾, which is due to Him. So He fulfilled your promise, granted you victory over your enemy, and gave you what was due. This was mentioned and preferred by al-Nahhas (al-Nahhas, grammarian).

It was also said that the *kaf* in "kama" is the *kaf* of comparison in the manner of recompense, like the saying of a person to his servant: "Just as I directed you against my enemies, and they overcame you, and you asked for reinforcement so I reinforced you and strengthened you and removed your weakness, so now seize them and punish them."

It was also said that the *kaf* is in the nominative position, as the predicate of an omitted subject, its estimated form being: "This state is like the state of your bringing out," meaning that their dislike of what you saw of distributing the spoils to the fighters is like their dislike of your going out to war. This was mentioned by the author of al-Kashshaf (al-Zamakhshari, author of al-Kashshaf). "In truth" is connected to an omitted element, and the estimate is: a bringing out accompanied by the truth which has no doubt in it.

The clause ﴿and indeed a group of the believers were averse﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (*hal*): that is, as He brought you out while they were averse to it. This is because when Allah promised them one of the two groups, either the caravan or the army, they desired the caravan because of the booty it contained and because it was safe from fighting, as will be explained later.

The clause ﴿they argue with you concerning the truth after it has become clear﴾ is either in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause following another circumstantial clause, or it is a new clause answering an implied question. Their argument concerned His commanding them to face one of the two groups; the caravan had escaped, and He commanded them to fight the army, while they did not have great readiness with them. Therefore it was hard for them, and they said: "If you had told us about the fighting, we would have taken equipment and completed our preparation." The meaning of "concerning the truth" is: concerning the fighting, after it had become clear to them that you do not command anything except by the permission of Allah, or after it had become clear to them that Allah had promised them victory over one of the two groups, and that if the caravan escaped, they would gain victory over the army. "After" is an adverbial of time governing "they argue with you," and *ma* is a verbal (infinitival) particle, meaning: they argue with you after the truth has become clear to them.

His saying: ﴿as if they were being driven toward death while they looked on﴾. The *kaf* is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause relating to the pronoun in "averse," meaning: in the state of their extreme terror of fighting, they resemble one who is being driven to be killed while he is watching the causes of his killing, looking at them, not doubting them.

His saying: ﴿And when Allah promised you one of the two groups, that it would be yours﴾. The adverbial phrase is in the accusative position governed by an omitted verb, meaning: remember the time when Allah promised you one of the two groups. He commanded them to remember the time, though the intention is to mention the events that occurred in it, for the sake of emphasis. The two groups are the caravan and the army. "One" is the second object of "promised," and "that it would be yours" is a substitute for it, a substitute of inclusion. Its meaning is: that it is subjected to you, that you will overcome it, take booty from it, and do with it what you wish of killing, capture, and plunder; they cannot repel you, and they cannot control for themselves any harm or benefit from you. In this clause there is a reminder to them of one of the blessings with which Allah favored them.

His saying: ﴿and you wished﴾ is conjoined to "He promises you," among the events whose times they were commanded to remember: that the group without the thorn (armed strength), which is the caravan group, would be yours rather than the group with the thorn, which is the army.

Abu 'Ubayda said: that is, the group without the edge.

*Al-shawka* means weapons, and *al-shawka* also means a plant that has a point, from which comes the phrase "a man sharp of weapons," meaning sharp-edged in weapons, then it is inverted to say "sharp of weapons." So *al-shawka* is used metaphorically from the single thorn. The meaning is: you wished to overcome the group that had no weapons, which is the caravan group, because it would be pure booty free from the turmoil of fighting, since there was no one with it to defend it.

His saying: ﴿and Allah wills to establish the truth by His words﴾ is conjoined to "you wished," and it is among the events whose times they were commanded to remember. That is: Allah wills something other than what you wish, namely to establish the truth by manifesting it, in accordance with what He decreed of your victory over the group with strength, their killing of their chieftains, the capture of many of them, and your seizing of the wealth they had brought against you, with which they sought to repel you. "The words" refer to the verses He revealed concerning fighting the group with strength, and His promise to them of victory over it. ﴿And cut off the last remnant of the disbelievers﴾: *dābir* is the last, and cutting it off is an expression for uprooting, meaning: He will entirely eradicate them.

His saying: ﴿so that He might establish the truth and nullify falsehood﴾. This clause is the reason for what Allah wills: that is, He willed that, or He wills that, in order to manifest the truth and raise it, and to nullify falsehood and abase it. Or the *lam* is connected to an omitted element: that is, He did that so that He might establish the truth. It was also said that it is connected to "He cuts off." This clause is not a repetition of what came before it, because the first clause explains the difference between the two wills, while this clause explains the wisdom that calls for it, the reason that requires it, and the benefit that results from it. "Establishing the truth" is making it manifest, and "nullifying falsehood" is annihilating it. ﴿Rather, We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it crushes it, and behold, it vanishes﴾ (al-Anbiya': 18). The object of ﴿though the criminals dislike it﴾ is omitted, meaning: though they dislike that He should establish the truth and nullify falsehood. The criminals are the polytheists of Quraysh, or all groups of disbelievers.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il (Dala'il al-Nubuwwa) have narrated from Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us while we were in Medina, and news had reached him that the caravan of Abu Sufyan had approached. He said: 'What do you think about it? Perhaps Allah will give it to us as booty and grant us safety.' So we set out. When we had travelled a day or two, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to count ourselves, and we did so, and we were three hundred and thirteen. We informed the Prophet ﷺ of our number, and he rejoiced at that and praised Allah and said: 'The number of the companions of Talut.' Then he said: 'What do you think about fighting the people? They have been informed of your departure.' We said: 'O Messenger of Allah, no, by Allah, we have no strength to fight the people; we only went out for the caravan.' Then he said: 'What do you think about fighting the people?' We said the same as before. Al-Miqdad said: 'Do not say as the people of Moses said to Moses: "So go, you and your Lord, and fight; indeed, we are sitting here" (al-Ma'ida: 24).' Then Allah revealed: ﴿As your Lord brought you out﴾ up to His saying: ﴿and when Allah promised you one of the two groups, that it would be yours﴾. When Allah promised us one of the two groups, either the people or the caravan, our hearts were content. Then we met the people, and we lined up. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'O Allah, I ask You to fulfill Your promise.' Then Ibn Rawaha said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I wish to advise you, though the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is too excellent to be advised. Indeed Allah is greater and more majestic than that you should ask Him to fulfill His promise.' He said: 'O son of Rawaha, I will indeed ask Allah to fulfill His promise, for Allah does not break His promise.' Then he took a handful of dust and threw it at the faces of the people, and they fled. Then Allah revealed: ﴿And you did not throw when you threw, but Allah threw﴾ (al-Anfal: 17). So we killed and captured. Then 'Umar said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I do not think you should have captives, for we are only to call and conciliate.' We said: 'O assembly of the Ansar, 'Umar says what he says only out of envy toward us.' Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ slept, then awoke and said: 'Call 'Umar to me.' He was called, and he said: 'Indeed Allah has revealed to me: ﴿It is not for a prophet to have captives﴾ (al-Anfal: 67), the verse.'" In its chain is Ibn Lahi'a, and concerning him there is a well-known discussion.

Ibn Abi Shayba in al-Musannaf and Ibn Mardawayh narrated, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Alqama ibn Waqqas al-Laythi, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out for Badr, and when he reached al-Rawha', he addressed the people and said: 'How do you see it?' Abu Bakr said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we have heard that they are so and so.' Then he addressed the people again and said: 'How do you see it?' 'Umar said the same as Abu Bakr's words. Then he addressed the people again and said: 'How do you see it?' Sa'd ibn Mu'adh said: 'O Messenger of Allah, is it us you mean? By Him who honored you and revealed the Book to you, I have never traveled this road, nor do I have knowledge of it. If you were to go until you reached Bark al-Ghimad of Yemen, we would indeed go with you, and we would not be like those who said to Moses: ﴿So go, you and your Lord, and fight; indeed, we are sitting here﴾ (al-Ma'ida: 24). Rather, go, you and your Lord, and fight; indeed, we are with you, following. Perhaps you set out for a matter and Allah has revealed to you something else. Look at what Allah has revealed to you and proceed with it. Join the ties of whomever you wish, sever the ties of whomever you wish, make enemies of whomever you wish, make peace with whomever you wish, and take from our wealth whatever you wish.' Then the Qur'an was revealed in accordance with the words of Sa'd: ﴿As your Lord brought you out of your house in truth﴾ up to His saying: ﴿and cut off the last remnant of the disbelievers﴾. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had only wished for the booty with Abu Sufyan, but Allah revealed to him fighting."

Ibn Abi Shayba, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid concerning His saying: ﴿As your Lord brought you out of your house in truth﴾: "Likewise they argue with you concerning the going out to fight."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from al-Suddi concerning His saying: ﴿As your Lord brought you out of your house in truth﴾: "It is the Prophet's ﷺ going out to Badr." ﴿And indeed a group of the believers were averse﴾: "To the pursuit of the polytheists." ﴿They argue with you concerning the truth after it has become clear﴾: "that you do nothing except what Allah has commanded you."

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 8, verses 9–10:

His saying: "when you sought help" (إذْ تَسْتَغِيثُونَ): the adverbial phrase is dependent on a deleted verb, meaning: "and remember the time of your seeking help." It has also been said that it is a substitute (badal) for ﴿when Allah promised you﴾ (al-Anfal: 8), governed by its own governing word; and it has been said that it is dependent on his saying "that He might establish the truth" (al-Anfal: 8). Al-istighathah (seeking help) is asking for relief (ghawth). It is said: "So-and-so sought help from me (istaghathani fulan), and I gave him help (faghathtuhu)," and the noun is al-ghiyath (help). The meaning is that when the Muslims knew that fighting the armed group (al-ta'ifah dhat al-shawkah), namely the unarmed-caravan-protectors (al-nafir), was unavoidable, as Allah had commanded them and willed it from them, and they saw the great number of the nafir and their own small number, they sought help from Allah, glorified is He. It is established in Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), that: "The number of the polytheists on the day of Badr was a thousand, and the number of the Muslims was three hundred and seventeen men, and when the Prophet (ﷺ) saw that, he faced the qiblah, then stretched out his hands and began to call upon his Lord: 'O Allah, fulfil for me what You have promised me. O Allah, give me what You have promised me. O Allah, if this band of the people of Islam perishes, You will not be worshipped on the earth,'" and the hadith continues.

"So He answered you" (فاسْتَجابَ لَكم) is coordinated upon "you sought help" (تَسْتَغِيثُونَ), included with it in the reminder. Although it is in the future form, it has the meaning of the past, and for this reason "answered" (استجاب) is coordinated upon it.

His saying: ﴿that I will reinforce you with a thousand of the angels﴾: that is, "that I am reinforcing you," so the preposition was deleted and the verb was connected to its object. It was read with a kasrah on the hamzah, on the intention of speech, or because "answered" (استجاب) carries the meaning of saying. His saying "murdifin" (مُرْدِفِينَ): Nafi' read it with a fathah on the dal, as a passive participle (ism maf'ul), and the rest read it with a kasrah, as an active participle (ism fa'il). It is in the accusative as a circumstantial (hal). The meaning according to the first reading is that He made some of them follow others, and according to the second reading that they were made to follow one another. It has been said that "murdifin" in both readings is an attribute (na't) of "a thousand". It has been said that on the first reading it is a circumstantial clause from the pronoun of the object in "mumiddukum" (reinforcing you): that is, reinforcing you while being followed by a thousand of the angels. It has been said that radifa and ardafa have the same meaning, but Abu Ubaydah denied this, saying: because of His saying, exalted is He, ﴿followed by the following one﴾ (al-Nazi'at: 7), and He did not say "al-murdafah".

Sibawayh said: In the verse there is a third reading, which is "murudhdhifin" with a dammah on the ra' and a kasrah on the dal, shaddah-ed, and a fourth reading with a fathah on the ra' and a shaddah on the dal.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad and Asim al-Jahdari read "bi-alaf" (with thousands), the plural of alf, and this agrees with what preceded in Al 'Imran.

The pronoun in "wa ma (p-528) ja'alahu Allah" refers to the reinforcement implied by His saying "Indi mumiddukum" (that I am reinforcing you), ﴿except as good tidings﴾: that is, only as good tidings to you of His victory. This is an exceptive construction (istithna' mufarragh): that is, Allah did not make your reinforcement for anything except as good tidings to you of victory, and so that your hearts might be reassured by it, that is, by the reinforcement. In this is an indication that the angels did not fight; rather Allah reinforced the Muslims with them as good tidings for them and to reassure and strengthen their hearts. The lam in "li-tatma'inna" (so that they might be reassured) is connected to a deleted verb that is to be understood as coming later: that is, and so that your hearts might be reassured He did this and for nothing else. ﴿And victory is only from the presence of Allah﴾, not from the presence of anyone else; the angels have no effect in that. He alone is the true Helper, and they were only one of the causes of victory which Allah ordained for you and with which He reinforced you. ﴿Indeed Allah is Almighty﴾, who cannot be overcome, ﴿All-Wise﴾ in all His acts.

Ibn Jarir reported from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: Jibril descended with a thousand angels on the right flank of the Prophet (ﷺ), and Abu Bakr was there, and Mika'il descended with a thousand angels on the left flank of the Prophet (ﷺ), and I was on the left.

Sunayd, Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh reported from Mujahid, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) was not reinforced with more than this thousand which Allah mentioned in al-Anfal, and He mentioned the three thousand and the five thousand only as good tidings.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh reported from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying "murdifin", that he said: "following one another (mutatabi'in)."

Ibn Jarir reported from him regarding His saying "murdifin" that he said: "the reinforcement (al-madad)."

Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh reported from him also, regarding the verse, that he said: "Behind every angel is an angel."

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from al-Sha'bi, who said: There were a thousand "murdifin" and three thousand "munzalin," so they were four thousand, and they were the reinforcement of the Muslims on their frontiers.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh reported from Mujahid regarding His saying "murdifin" that he said: "striving (mujiddin)."

Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir reported from Qatadah, who said: "Following one another. Allah reinforced them with a thousand, then with three, then completed them to five thousand." ﴿And Allah made it not but as good tidings for you, and so that your hearts might be reassured by it﴾, he said: that is, the descent of the angels.

He said: It was also mentioned to us that Umar said: "As for the day of Badr, we have no doubt that the angels were with us; as for after that, Allah knows best."

Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh reported from Ibn Zayd, regarding "murdifin", that he said: "some of them following on the trail of others."

**Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 8, verses 11–14:**

His saying, ﴿when He covered you﴾: the adverbial phrase (al-zarf) is in the accusative, governed by a verb understood, like the one before it, or it is a second substitute (badal) for ﴿when He promised you﴾, or it is in the accusative governed by the "victory" (al-nasr) mentioned before it. Anything other than this is weak and has no basis. The reading ﴿yughashshikum﴾ (He covers you, with the verb having Allah as its subject) is the reading of Nafi' and the people of Madina. This reading corresponds to what comes before it, namely His saying, ﴿Victory is only from Allah﴾, and to what comes after it, namely ﴿and He sends down upon you﴾. So the speech is coherent and fitting.

*Al-zahf* (the advance of troops) means drawing near gradually, little by little. Its original sense is pushing forward on the buttocks, and then every person walking toward another in battle was called *zahif* (advancing). *Al-tazahuf* means approaching and drawing close. You say: *zahafa ila al-'aduww zahfan* (he advanced toward the enemy in an advance), and *izdahafa al-qawm* (the people advanced), meaning some of them walked toward others. The accusative *zahfan* may be either a verbal noun for a verb that is omitted, meaning *tazhafuna zahfan* (you advance in an advance), or a circumstantial clause (*hal*) referring to the believers, meaning while you are advancing toward the unbelievers; or a circumstantial clause referring to those who disbelieved, meaning while the unbelievers are advancing toward you; or a circumstantial clause referring to both parties, meaning mutually advancing. ﴿So do not turn your backs to them﴾. God forbade the believers to flee from the unbelievers when they meet them, and when some of them have moved toward others for combat. The apparent meaning of this verse is general, covering all believers at all times and in all circumstances, except the case of *taharruf* (maneuvering) and *tahayyuz* (withdrawing to a group).

It has been reported from 'Umar, Ibn 'Umar, Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Hurayrah, Abu Sa'id, Abu Nadrah, 'Ikrimah, Nafi', al-Hasan, Qatadah, Zayd ibn Abi Habib, and al-Dahhak that the prohibition on fleeing from the advance in this verse is specific to the Day of Badr, and that the people of Badr were not permitted to withdraw. Had they withdrawn, they would have withdrawn to the polytheists, since on that day there were no Muslims on earth other than themselves, and they had no *fi'ah* (group) except the Prophet ﷺ. After that, however, some of them became a *fi'ah* for others. This is also the view of Abu Hanifah.

They said: This is supported by His saying: ﴿And whoever turns his back to them on that day﴾, for it refers to the Day of Badr. It has also been said that this verse is abrogated (*mansukhah*) by the verse of weakness (*ayat al-di'f*).

Most scholars held that this verse is *muhkamah* (firm and not abrogated), general and not specific, and that fleeing from the advance is forbidden. This is supported by the fact that this verse was revealed after the battle of Badr had ended.

As for the first group's view, it is answered that the reference in *yawma'idhin* (on that day) to the Day of Badr is not correct, since the reference is to the day of the advance, as the context indicates. There is no contradiction between this verse and the verse of weakness; rather, this verse is qualified by it, so fleeing from the advance is forbidden under the condition that God specified in the verse of weakness. There is no basis for what they said, that there were no Muslims on earth on the Day of Badr other than those who were present there, for in Medina at that time there was a large number of people whom the Prophet ﷺ did not order to go out, because he and those who went out with him did not initially think that there would be fighting.

This is supported by the authentic reports that explicitly state that fleeing from the advance is among the major sins (*al-kaba'ir*), as in the hadith: "Avoid the seven destructive sins," and within it: "and turning away on the day of the advance," and similar hadiths. This topic has long ramifications and many branches, and it is explained in its proper places.

Ibn 'Atiyyah said: *al-adbar* is the plural of *dubur* (back), and the expression "back" in this verse is eloquent, because of the disgrace it implies for the fleeing man and the blame directed at him.

His saying: ﴿except one who maneuvers for combat﴾. *Al-taharruf* is departing from the straight direction. What is meant here is moving from one side to another in the battlefield, seeking the stratagems of war and deceiving the enemy. It includes feigning defeat so that the enemy pursues, then turning back on them and gaining control over them, and similar war tactics, for war is deception.

His saying: ﴿or one who withdraws to a group﴾, that is, to a group of Muslims other than the group facing the enemy. The accusative of *muta-harrifan* and *mutahayyizan* is by exception from those who turn away, meaning: whoever turns his back to them, except a man of theirs who maneuvers or withdraws. They may also be in the accusative as circumstantial clauses, and the particle of exception would then be *laghw* (superfluous) with no governing function. The clause ﴿he has earned wrath from God﴾ is the answer to the condition.

The meaning is: whoever flees and retreats from the advance has returned with wrath from God, except one who maneuvers or withdraws. ﴿And his refuge is Hell﴾, that is, the place to which he retreats is the Fire. Thus his flight leads him to something more severe in affliction than what he fled from, and greater in punishment.

*Al-ma'wa* is the place to which a person retreats. ﴿And wretched is the destination﴾ means what he arrives at is the torment of the Fire.

This verse includes this severe threat for whoever flees from the advance, and in this is evidence that it is among the destructive major sins.

His saying: ﴿So you did not kill them, but God killed them﴾. The *fa'* (so) is the answer to an implied condition, meaning: if you know what God has related to you of His aid to you with angels and His casting terror into their hearts, then you did not kill them, but God killed them through the means He facilitated for you that necessitate victory.

His saying: ﴿And you did not throw when you threw, but God threw﴾.

It has been reported from Malik that what is meant is what the Prophet ﷺ did on the Day of Hunayn, when he threw a handful of pebbles from the valley at the polytheists, and it struck each one of them. It has also been said that what is meant is the throw by which the Messenger of God ﷺ struck Ubayy ibn Khalaf in the neck with a spear, and he fled and died from it. It has also been said that what is meant is the arrow that the Messenger of God ﷺ shot at the fortress of Khaybar, and it traveled through the air until it struck Ibn Abi al-Huqayq while he was on his bed. These views are weak, for the verse was revealed right after the battle of Badr.

Also, the well-known account in the books of biography (*siyar*) and hadith about the killing of Ibn Abi al-Huqayq is that it occurred in a different form from this.

The correct view, as Ibn Ishaq and others said, is that the throwing mentioned in this verse is what the Prophet ﷺ did on the Day of Badr, for he took a handful of dust and threw it into the faces of the polytheists, and it struck each one of them and entered their eyes, nostrils and noses.

Abu 'Ubaydah also related something similar in *Kitab al-Majaz*.

Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Mubarrad said: The meaning of ﴿And you did not throw﴾ is by your own strength, ﴿when you threw﴾, but rather by the strength of God you threw. Rather, it was God's throw, since it produced that great effect. Thus He affirmed the throwing to the Messenger of God ﷺ because its form was produced by him, and He negated it from him because its effect, which no human can bear, is the act of God, Mighty and Majestic. So God is the true agent of the throw, as though it had never existed from the Messenger of God ﷺ at all. Thus it is in *al-Kashshaf*.

The reference in His saying ﴿that﴾ is to the good trial, and it is in the nominative case as the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: the purpose is ﴿that﴾. ﴿And that God is the one who weakens the plot of the unbelievers﴾, meaning: its purpose from Him, glorified is He, by what occurred of what the preceding verses related, is to test the believers and to weaken the plot of the unbelievers. It has also been said that what is referred to is the killing and the throwing.

It has been read with the *ha'* (in *muhinu*) doubled and with it single with tanwin. Al-Hasan read it with the *ha'* single and in construct form (idafah).

*Al-kayd* is scheming, and its explanation has already preceded.

Al-Bukhari in his *Tarikh*, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh reported from Nafi' that he asked Ibn 'Umar, saying: "We are a people who do not stand firm when fighting our enemy, and we do not know who the *fi'ah* is in front of us, or our army?" He said to me: "The *fi'ah* is the Messenger of God ﷺ." I said: "God says: ﴿When you meet those who disbelieve advancing, do not turn your backs to them﴾." He said: "This verse was only revealed about the people of Badr, not before it nor after it."

'Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Nahhas in his *Nasikh*, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Hakim, and Ibn Mardawayh reported from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri concerning His saying: ﴿And whoever turns his back to them on that day﴾, the verse, that he said: "It was only for the people of Badr specifically."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab who said: "Do not let this verse deceive you, for it was only on the Day of Badr, and I am a *fi'ah* for every Muslim."

Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh reported from Ibn 'Abbas concerning the verse, that he said: "It was revealed specifically about the people of Badr, that it was not permitted for them to flee from the Messenger of God ﷺ and abandon him."

It has been reported that the restriction of this verse to the people of Badr is from a group of the Successors (*tabi'un*) and those after them, and we have already mentioned this.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh reported from Sa'id ibn Jubayr concerning His saying: ﴿except one who maneuvers for combat﴾, that he said: "That means one who feigns retreat, intending to return to attack the polytheists." ﴿or withdraws to a group﴾, that is, or withdraws to his companions without having been defeated. ﴿then he has earned wrath from God﴾, that is, they deserved anger from God. ﴿And his refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination﴾. He said: "This was specifically on the Day of Badr, and it was severe for the Muslims on that day, so that He might cut off the remnant of the unbelievers. It was the first battle in which the Muslims fought the polytheists of Mecca."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from al-Dahhak, who said: "The *mutaharrif* is one who advances ahead of his companions, who sees a weakness in the enemy and strikes it. The *mutahayyiz* is one who flees to the Messenger of God ﷺ, and likewise whoever flees today to his commander and his companions."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Abu al-Shaykh reported from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah concerning His saying: ﴿And whoever turns his back to them on that day﴾, that he said: "This verse is abrogated by the verse in al-Anfal: ﴿Now God has lightened [the burden] for you﴾ (al-Anfal: 66), the verse."

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Sa'd, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, 'Abd ibn Humayd, al-Bukhari in *al-Adab al-Mufrad* (and the wording is his), Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, who graded it *hasan*, Ibn Majah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Nahhas, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in *Shu'ab al-Iman* reported from Ibn 'Umar, who said: "We were on a military campaign, and the people panicked and fled in confusion. We said: How can we meet the Messenger of God ﷺ when we have fled from the advance and returned with wrath? So we came to the Messenger of God before the dawn prayer. He came out and said: 'Who are the people?' We said: 'We are the fleeing ones.' He said: 'No, rather you are the returning ones (*al-'akkarun*).' We kissed his hand, and he said: 'I am your *fi'ah*, and I am the *fi'ah* of the Muslims.' Then he recited: ﴿except one who maneuvers for combat or withdraws to a group﴾."

Hadiths have been reported prohibiting fleeing from the advance and stating that it is among the major sins, and a group of the Companions reported that it is among the major sins, as Ibn Jarir reported from Ibn 'Abbas.

Ibn Abi Shaybah reported from Ibn 'Umar.

Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh reported from Mujahid concerning His saying: ﴿So you did not kill them﴾, that he said: "This was said to the Companions of Muhammad ﷺ when they said: 'I killed this one, and I killed that one.'" ﴿And you did not throw when you threw﴾ was said to Muhammad ﷺ when he threw pebbles at the unbelievers.

'Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn al-Mundhir reported from Qatadah concerning His saying: ﴿And you did not throw when you threw﴾, that he said: "He threw at them with pebbles on the Day of Badr."

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 8, verse 15–18 (part 2 of 2):

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Hakim ibn Hizam, who said: "When the Day of Badr came, we heard a sound from the sky to the earth (p-532), as if it were the sound of a pebble falling into a basin. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) threw that gravel and said: 'May the faces be disfigured!' and we were routed. This is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And you did not throw when you threw, but Allah threw﴾, the verse."

Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Jabir, who said: "I heard the sound of pebbles falling from the sky on the Day of Badr, as if they had fallen into a basin. When the people lined up, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took them and threw them into the faces of the polytheists, and they fled. This is His saying: ﴿And you did not throw when you threw, but Allah threw.﴾"

al-Tabarani and Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated "from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And you did not throw when you threw﴾, he said: The Messenger of Allah said to Ali: 'Hand me a handful of gravel.' So he handed it to him, and he threw it into the faces of the people, and not one of the people remained except that his eyes were filled with the gravel. Then this verse was revealed: ﴿And you did not throw when you threw.﴾"

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, who said: "When the Day of Uhud came, Ubayy ibn Khalaf began to spur his horse until he came near the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and some men of the Muslims intercepted Ubayy ibn Khalaf to kill him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: 'Hold back!' So they held back. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took his spear in his hand and threw it at Ubayy ibn Khalaf, and it broke one of his ribs. Ubayy ibn Khalaf returned to his companions, heavy (wounded), and they carried him when they turned back, returning. They began saying: 'There is no harm.' Ubayy said when they said that to him: 'By Allah, if it had been among the people, it would have killed them. Did he not say: I will kill you, if Allah wills?' His companions took him along, supporting him, until he died in part of the way, and they buried him." Ibn al-Musayyib said: "Concerning that, Allah revealed: ﴿And you did not throw when you threw.﴾"

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib and al-Zuhri something similar to it, and its chain of transmission to both of them is sound. Al-Hakim also narrated it in al-Mustadrak.

Ibn Kathir said: This statement from these two imams is very strange, and perhaps they meant that the verse encompasses them through its generality. Likewise said Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, as will come.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr: "That on the Day of Ibn Abi al-Huqayq, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called for a bow and shot with it at the fortress, and the arrow came until it killed Ibn Abi al-Huqayq in his bed. So Allah revealed: ﴿And you did not throw when you threw, but Allah threw.﴾"

Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr regarding His saying: ﴿But Allah threw﴾, i.e., that throw was not by your throwing, were it not for what Allah made of your victory and what He cast into the hearts of your enemy, until He routed them. ﴿And that He might test the believers with a fine trial from Him﴾, i.e., that the believers might recognize from His blessing upon them in granting them victory over their enemy despite the abundance of their enemy and the fewness of their number, so that by that they might know His right and give thanks for His blessing.
