When God commanded fighting with His words, ﴿And fight them until there is no more fitnah﴾ (al-Anfal: 39), and fighting was the likely occasion for acquiring spoils (ghanimah), He mentioned the ruling on spoils. We have already noted that the original meaning of ghanimah (spoils) is acquiring sheep (ghanam) from the enemy. Then the term was used for everything obtained from them, and it may be used for everything gained through effort. Among its uses is the words of the poet:

(p-540) I have wandered through the horizons until I was content with the spoils of returning [home safely].

Similar to it is the words of another:

The one who feeds on spoils, on the day of spoils, his food is [assured] wherever he turns, while the one who is deprived remains deprived.

As for the meaning of ghanimah in the Sharia, al-Qurtubi reported a consensus that what is meant by God's words, ﴿And know that whatever you acquire of anything﴾, is the property of the disbelievers when the Muslims gain victory over them by force and domination. He said: The linguistic usage does not require this restriction, but the Sharia usage restricted the term to this type.

Ibn 'Abd al-Barr claimed a consensus that this verse came after His words, ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾ (al-Anfal: 1), and that four-fifths of the spoils are divided among those who took them. He said that His words, ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾, were revealed when the people of Badr disputed over the spoils of Badr, as was mentioned at the beginning of the surah. It has been said that this verse, meaning His words ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾, is muhkam (definitive) and not abrogated, and that the spoils belong to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and are not divided among those who took them; likewise for the imams after him. Al-Mawardi related this from many of the Malikis, who said: the imam may withhold it from them. They argued with the conquest of Makkah and the story of Hunayn. Abu 'Ubaydah used to say: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) conquered Makkah by force, conferred favour upon its people, returned it to them, did not divide it, and did not make it fay'. A group of scholars has reported a consensus that four-fifths of the spoils belong to those who took them, and among those who reported this were Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn 'Abd al-Barr, al-Dawudi, al-Mazari, al-Qadi 'Iyad, and Ibn al-'Arabi. The narrations concerning the division of spoils among those who took them and its manner are very numerous indeed.

Al-Qurtubi said: As far as I know, no one has said that His words, ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾ and so on, abrogate His words, ﴿And know that whatever you acquire of anything﴾ and so on. Rather, the majority said that His words, ﴿And know that whatever you acquire of anything﴾, are the abrogating text, and they are the ones upon whom alteration or substitution of the Book of God is not permitted.

As for the story of the conquest of Makkah, there is no proof in it because the scholars differ over whether it was conquered by force. He said: As for the story of Hunayn, he compensated the Ansar when they said: "You give the spoils to Quraysh and leave us, while our swords still drip with their blood." So he said to them, as in Muslim and others: "Are you not content that the people return with worldly goods while you return with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to your homes?" No one other than him may say this statement; rather, it is specific to him.

His words, ﴿whatever you acquire of anything﴾, include everything to which the name ghanimah applies. The phrase ﴿of anything﴾ explains the relative pronoun "ma" (whatever). Consensus has specified from the generality of the verse the captives, for the choice concerning them rests with the imam without disagreement. Likewise the spoils (salab) of a slain enemy when the imam announces it. It has been said that the conquered land is likewise, and this was refuted on the grounds that there is no consensus concerning land.

His words, ﴿then to God belongs its fifth﴾: al-Nakha'i read "fa-inna li-Llah" with the letter "inna" pronounced with a kasra.

The rest read it with a fatha on "inna", so that "anna" and what follows it is a subject (mubtada'), and its predicate is omitted. The estimated meaning is: then it is right or obligatory that to God belongs its fifth.

The scholars have differed over the manner of dividing the fifth (khumus) according to six opinions.

The first: A group said: The fifth is divided into six parts, and one sixth is set aside for the Ka'bah, which is what belongs to God; the second for the Messenger of God; the third for the kinsfolk (dhu al-qurba); the fourth for the orphans; the fifth for the needy; and the sixth for the wayfarer (ibn al-sabil).

The second opinion, held by Abu al-'Aliyah and al-Rabi': The spoils are divided into five parts. One part is set aside, and four parts are divided among those who took them. Then he puts his hand into the part he set aside, and whatever he takes from it he gives to the Ka'bah. Then he divides the remainder of the part he set aside into five: for the Messenger and those after him, according to the verse.

The third opinion: It is reported from Zayn al-'Abidin 'Ali ibn al-Husayn that he said: "The fifth belongs to us." It was said to him: "God says, ﴿and the orphans and the needy and the wayfarer﴾." He said: "Our orphans, our needy, and the sons of our wayfarers."

The fourth opinion, the view of al-Shafi'i: The fifth is divided into five parts. The share of God and the share of His Messenger are one share, spent on the interests of the believers. The four-fifths are for the four categories mentioned in the verse.

The fifth opinion, the view of Abu Hanifah: The fifth is divided into three: the orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer. The ruling concerning the kinship of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) ended with his death, just as the ruling concerning his share ended.

He said: From the fifth one begins with the repair of bridges, the building of mosques, and the provisions of judges and soldiers. Something similar to this is also reported from al-Shafi'i.

The sixth opinion, the view of Malik: It is left to the judgment and discretion of the imam, who takes from it without fixed measure, gives to the fighters from it according to his discretion, and spends the remainder on the interests of the Muslims.

Al-Qurtubi said: This is also the view of the four Caliphs, and they acted upon it. It is indicated by the saying of the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "I have nothing from what God has bestowed upon you as fay' except the fifth, and the fifth is returned to you." For he did not divide it into fifths or thirds. He only mentioned what is in the verse to draw attention to them, because they are among the most important of those to whom it is given.

Al-Zajjaj said, arguing for this opinion: God says, ﴿They ask you what they should spend. Say: Whatever good you spend is for the parents and the near relatives and the orphans and the needy and the wayfarer﴾ (al-Baqarah: 215). It is permissible by consensus to spend it on other than these categories if one sees fit.

His words, ﴿and for the near kinsfolk (dhi al-qurba)﴾: It has been said that repeating the preposition "li" before dhi al-qurba, but not before those after them, is to remove the assumption that they share in the Prophet's (ﷺ) share.

The scholars have differed concerning "al-qurba" (the near kin) according to several opinions. The first is that they are all of Quraysh. This was related from some of the early scholars, and it was used as evidence by the report that "the Prophet (ﷺ), when he ascended al-Safa, began calling out to all the clans of Quraysh, saying: 'O sons of so-and-so, O sons of so-and-so.'"

Al-Shafi'i, Ahmad, Abu Thawr, Mujahid, Qatadah, Ibn Jurayj, and Muslim ibn Khalid said: They are the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib, due to the saying of the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "The Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib are one thing," and he interlaced his fingers. It is in the Sahih. It was also said: They are the Banu Hashim alone. This was the view of Malik, al-Thawri, al-Awza'i and others, and it is related from 'Ali ibn al-Husayn and Mujahid.

His words, ﴿if you have believed in God﴾: al-Zajjaj said, from a group: The meaning is "Know that God is your Protector, if you have believed in God." Another group said: "in" is connected to His words, ﴿and know that whatever you acquire﴾. Ibn 'Atiyah said: This is the correct view, because His words "and know" contain a command to submit and accept the command of God regarding the spoils. So "in" (if) is linked to "and know" with this meaning: that is, if you are believers in God, then submit and accept God's command regarding the spoils, in what He has informed you of concerning the manner of dividing the spoils.

In al-Kashshaf it says: It is connected to an omitted element indicated by "and know", meaning: if you have believed in God, then know that the fifth of the spoils must be drawn near to God through, so cut off your desires concerning it, and be content with the four-fifths. The intended knowledge is not bare knowledge, but knowledge that includes action and obedience to God's command, because bare knowledge is equal for the believer and the disbeliever. End.

His words, ﴿and what We sent down upon Our servant﴾: It is conjoined to the divine name: that is, if you have believed in God and in what We sent down. ﴿The day of the Criterion﴾ is the day of Badr, because it distinguished between the people of truth and the people of falsehood. ﴿The two hosts﴾ are the two groups of Muslims and disbelievers. ﴿And God is over all things competent﴾. Among His great power is the victory of the smaller group over the larger.

His words, ﴿when you were on the near side of the valley and they were on the far side﴾: Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, and Ya'qub read "al-'udwah" with a kasra on the 'ayn in both places, and the rest read it with a damma. "Idh" is a substitute (badal) for ﴿the day of the Criterion﴾, and it is permissible for the governing element to be omitted: that is, remember when you were.

Al-'Udwah means the side of the valley. "Al-dunya" is the feminine of "al-adna" (nearer), and "al-quswa" is the feminine of "al-aqsa" (farther), from "dana yadna" and "qasa yaqsu". It is said "al-qusya" as well, and the original is with a waw. This is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz. The near side was the side toward Madinah, and the far side was the side toward Makkah.

The meaning: at the time of your encampment on the nearer side of the valley toward Madinah, and your enemy on its farther side, toward Makkah.

The clause ﴿and the caravan was lower than you﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal). The accusative of ﴿asfal﴾ is as an adverb of place (zarf), and its position is nominative as a predicate: that is, while the caravan was in a place lower than the place where you were.

Al-Akhfash, al-Kisa'i and al-Farra' permitted the nominative "asfalu" in the sense of "more low than you". "Al-rakb" is the plural of "rakib" (rider), and the Arabs do not say "rakb" except for a group of riders on camels. It is not said of one on a horse or other mounts. Ibn Faris said the same, and Ibn al-Sikkit related it from most of the lexicographers.

The meaning of "al-rakb" here is the caravan of Abu Sufyan, which is what is meant by "the caravan" (al-'ir), for they were in a place lower than them, toward the seashore.

It has been said: The benefit of mentioning this condition in which they were, being on the near side while their enemy was on the far side, with the caravan lower than them, is to indicate the strength of the enemy's position and power. This is because the far side where the polytheists camped had water in it and was land without any dry ground, while the near side was soft, where feet sank, with no water. The caravan was behind the enemy's back along with the enemy's great numbers. So God bestowed favour upon the Muslims by granting them victory over them in that condition.

His words, ﴿And if you had made a mutual appointment, you would have differed concerning the appointment﴾: That is, if you and the polytheists of Makkah had made a mutual appointment to meet at this place for battle, some of you would have disagreed with others. Your fewness and their great numbers would have deterred you from fulfilling the appointment, and what was in their hearts of awe of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) would have deterred them. But God brought you together in this encounter ﴿so that God might accomplish a matter that was [already] to be done﴾: that is, something deserving to be done by Him, namely the victory of His allies, the abasement of His enemies, the honouring of His religion, and the humbling of disbelief. He brought out the Muslims to seize the caravan and its spoils, in their own estimation, and brought out the disbelievers to defend it. It was not in the reckoning of either party that this encounter would take place in this manner. The "li" in ﴿li-yaqdiya﴾ is connected to an omitted element; the estimated meaning is: He gathered them in order that He might accomplish.

The clause ﴿that he who perished might perish by clear evidence and he who lived might live by clear evidence﴾ is a substitute (badal) for the clause before it: that is, so that whoever dies, dies upon clear evidence, and whoever lives, lives upon clear evidence, so that no one will have an argument against God. It has been said: "Perishing" and "living" are metaphors for disbelief and Islam, meaning that the Islam of whoever embraced Islam should proceed from clear evidence and certainty that it is the religion of truth, and the disbelief of whoever disbelieved should proceed from clear evidence and not from the intrusion of doubt.

Nafi', Khalaf, Sahl, Ya'qub, al-Bazzi, and Abu Bakr read "man hayya" with two yas, according to the original. The rest read with one ya, by assimilation (idgham). This is the choice of Abu 'Ubayd because it is written so in the Mushaf.

His words, ﴿and indeed God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾: that is, He hears the disbelief of the disbelievers and knows it, and He hears the faith of the believers and knows it.

Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Abbad ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: Then he set out the divisions of the fay' (spoils, here meaning the booty), and said: ﴿And know that whatever you gain as booty﴾ after what had already passed at Badr, ﴿then to Allah belongs one-fifth of it﴾, to the end of the verse.

Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and al-Hakim narrated from Qays ibn Muslim al-Jadali, who said: I asked al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, Ibn al-Hanafiyyah, about the words of Allah: ﴿And know that whatever you gain as booty, then to Allah belongs one-fifth of it﴾. He said: This is the key to the speech (miftah kalam, an introductory phrase that opens the sentence). ﴿To Allah belongs the world and the Hereafter﴾, ﴿and to the Messenger and to the near of kin﴾. After the death of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they disagreed about these two shares. One of them said: the share of the near of kin is for the kinsmen of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Another of them said: the share of the near of kin is for the kinsmen of the Caliph. Another of them said: the share of the Prophet (ﷺ) is for the Caliph after him. The opinion of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came together on making these two shares for horses and equipment in the way of Allah. That was in the caliphate of Abu Bakr and Umar.

Ibn Jarir, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent out a raiding party (sariyyah) and they gained booty, he would divide the booty into five and set aside that for his fifth," and then he recited: ﴿And know that whatever you gain...﴾ to the end of the verse. He said: His words ﴿then to Allah belongs one-fifth of it﴾ are the key to the speech: ﴿to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾. So Allah made the share of Allah and of the Messenger one share. ﴿And to the near of kin﴾: He made these two shares a strength for horses and weapons. And He made the share of orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer not to be given to anyone else. And He made the remaining four shares: one share for the horse, one share for its rider, and one share for the foot soldier.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him, who said: The booty was divided into five fifths. Four of them were among those who fought for it, and one fifth was divided into four parts: a quarter for Allah, for the Messenger, and for the near kin (dhu al-qurba), meaning the kinsmen of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Whatever was for Allah and the Messenger went to the kinsmen of the Prophet (ﷺ), and the Prophet (ﷺ) took nothing from the fifth. The second quarter was for the orphans, the third quarter (p-542) for the needy, and the fourth quarter for the wayfarer, who is the poor guest who stops among the Muslims.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Abu al-Aliyah concerning His words: ﴿And know that whatever you gain as booty﴾, to the end of the verse. He said: "The booty would be brought and placed down, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would divide it into five shares. He would set aside one share from it, and divide the four shares among the people, meaning among those who witnessed the battle. Then he would put his hand into the entire share he had set aside, and whatever he grasped from it he would give to the Kaʿbah. That is what Allah named: ﴿Do not assign to Allah a share, for to Allah belongs the world and the Hereafter.﴾ Then he would turn to the rest of that share and divide it into five parts: one share for the Prophet (ﷺ), one share for the near kin, one share for the orphans, one share for the needy, and one share for the wayfarer."

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) would set aside the share of Allah for the weapons, the horses, the way of Allah, the covering of the Kaʿbah, its perfume, and whatever the Kaʿbah needed. He would set aside the share of the Messenger for horses, weapons, and the maintenance of his household. The share of the near kin was for his kinsmen, which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would place among them together with their share among the people. For the orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer there were three shares, which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would place with whomever he wished, wherever he wished. The Banu Abd al-Muttalib have no part in these three shares, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had one share among the shares of the people."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Husayn al-Muʿallim, who said: I asked Abd Allah ibn Buraydah about the words: ﴿then to Allah belongs one-fifth of it, and to the Messenger﴾. He said: What belongs to Allah is for His Prophet, and what belongs to the Messenger is for his wives.

Al-Shafiʿi, Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Muslim, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated from Ibn Abbas that Najdah wrote to him asking him about the near kin whom Allah mentioned. He wrote back: "We used to see that they were us. But our people refused this for us, and said: all of Quraysh are near kin." The addition of his words "and they said: all of Quraysh are near kin" was transmitted by Abu Masharr alone, and in it there is weakness.

Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated by another route from Ibn Abbas that Najdah al-Haruri sent to him asking him about the share of the near kin, and saying: "To whom do you see it belonging?" Ibn Abbas said: It is for the kinsmen of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) allotted to them. Umar had proposed to us something of that, a proposal we saw as below our right, so we returned it to them and refused to accept it. He had offered them that he would help their unmarried men marry, that he would pay the debts of their indebted, and that he would give to their poor, but he refused to give them more than that.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: "I have spared you the washings of the hands, because for you in the fifth of the fifth there is what suffices you or makes you independent."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated this from Ibrahim ibn Mahdi al-Misisi, who said: al-Muʿtamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us from his father, from Hanash, from Ikrimah, from him, as a marfuʿ (traced to the Prophet ﷺ) report.

Ibn Kathir said: This is a hadith with a good chain (hasan al-isnad). Ibrahim ibn Mahdi was judged reliable by Abu Hatim, but Yahya ibn Maʿin said: He brings forth strange reports (manakir).

Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from al-Zuhri and Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, from Jubayr ibn Mutʿim: "The Prophet (ﷺ) divided the share of the near kin from Khaybar among the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib." He said: I and Uthman ibn Affan walked until we entered upon him, and we said: "O Messenger of Allah, these are your brothers from the Banu Hashim. We do not deny their merit because of your standing among them. But what about our brothers from the Banu al-Muttalib, whom you gave preference over us, when we and they are on the same level in lineage?" He said: "They have never separated from us, in the Jahiliyyah or in Islam."

Muslim has also narrated it in his Sahih.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: The family of Muhammad who were given the fifth are: the family of Ali, the family of al-Abbas, the family of Jafar, and the family of Aqil.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) had one item from the spoils which he would select for himself, either a servant or a horse. After that, he would take his share from the fifth.

Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ali, who said: "I said: O Messenger of Allah, would you not appoint me over what Allah has specified for us from the fifth? So he appointed me over it."

Al-Hakim narrated it and graded it sound (sahhahahu), from him, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) appointed me over the fifth of the fifth, and I placed it in its proper places during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and during the times of Abu Bakr and Umar."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas concerning His words: ﴿the Day of the Criterion (yawm al-furqan)﴾. He said: It is the Day of Badr, and Badr is between Makkah and Madinah.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim (who graded it sound), Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dalail narrated from Ibn Abbas concerning His words: ﴿the Day of the Criterion﴾. He said: It is the Day of Badr, on which Allah separated truth from falsehood.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: The Night of the Criterion was the night when the two hosts met. Its morning was the night of Friday, on the seventeenth day that had passed of Ramadan. Ibn Jarir also narrated it from him.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Abbas concerning His words: ﴿when you were on the nearer side of the valley (al-ʿudwah al-dunya)﴾. He said: "The nearer side of the valley is the edge of the wadi." ﴿And the caravan was lower than you﴾: he said, that was Abu Sufyan.

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ikrimah, who said: "The nearer side (al-ʿudwah al-dunya) is the nearer bank of the valley, and the farther side (al-ʿudwah al-quswa) is the farther bank of the valley."

When God commanded fighting with His words, ﴿And fight them until there is no more fitnah﴾ (al-Anfal: 39), and fighting was the likely occasion for acquiring spoils (ghanimah), He mentioned the ruling on spoils. We have already noted that the original meaning of ghanimah (spoils) is acquiring sheep (ghanam) from the enemy. Then the term was used for everything obtained from them, and it may be used for everything gained through effort. Among its uses is the words of the poet:

(p-540) I have wandered through the horizons until I was content with the spoils of returning [home safely].

Similar to it is the words of another:

The one who feeds on spoils, on the day of spoils, his food is [assured] wherever he turns, while the one who is deprived remains deprived.

As for the meaning of ghanimah in the Sharia, al-Qurtubi reported a consensus that what is meant by God's words, ﴿And know that whatever you acquire of anything﴾, is the property of the disbelievers when the Muslims gain victory over them by force and domination. He said: The linguistic usage does not require this restriction, but the Sharia usage restricted the term to this type.

Ibn 'Abd al-Barr claimed a consensus that this verse came after His words, ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾ (al-Anfal: 1), and that four-fifths of the spoils are divided among those who took them. He said that His words, ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾, were revealed when the people of Badr disputed over the spoils of Badr, as was mentioned at the beginning of the surah. It has been said that this verse, meaning His words ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾, is muhkam (definitive) and not abrogated, and that the spoils belong to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and are not divided among those who took them; likewise for the imams after him. Al-Mawardi related this from many of the Malikis, who said: the imam may withhold it from them. They argued with the conquest of Makkah and the story of Hunayn. Abu 'Ubaydah used to say: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) conquered Makkah by force, conferred favour upon its people, returned it to them, did not divide it, and did not make it fay'. A group of scholars has reported a consensus that four-fifths of the spoils belong to those who took them, and among those who reported this were Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn 'Abd al-Barr, al-Dawudi, al-Mazari, al-Qadi 'Iyad, and Ibn al-'Arabi. The narrations concerning the division of spoils among those who took them and its manner are very numerous indeed.

Al-Qurtubi said: As far as I know, no one has said that His words, ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾ and so on, abrogate His words, ﴿And know that whatever you acquire of anything﴾ and so on. Rather, the majority said that His words, ﴿And know that whatever you acquire of anything﴾, are the abrogating text, and they are the ones upon whom alteration or substitution of the Book of God is not permitted.

As for the story of the conquest of Makkah, there is no proof in it because the scholars differ over whether it was conquered by force. He said: As for the story of Hunayn, he compensated the Ansar when they said: "You give the spoils to Quraysh and leave us, while our swords still drip with their blood." So he said to them, as in Muslim and others: "Are you not content that the people return with worldly goods while you return with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to your homes?" No one other than him may say this statement; rather, it is specific to him.

His words, ﴿whatever you acquire of anything﴾, include everything to which the name ghanimah applies. The phrase ﴿of anything﴾ explains the relative pronoun "ma" (whatever). Consensus has specified from the generality of the verse the captives, for the choice concerning them rests with the imam without disagreement. Likewise the spoils (salab) of a slain enemy when the imam announces it. It has been said that the conquered land is likewise, and this was refuted on the grounds that there is no consensus concerning land.

His words, ﴿then to God belongs its fifth﴾: al-Nakha'i read "fa-inna li-Llah" with the letter "inna" pronounced with a kasra.

The rest read it with a fatha on "inna", so that "anna" and what follows it is a subject (mubtada'), and its predicate is omitted. The estimated meaning is: then it is right or obligatory that to God belongs its fifth.

The scholars have differed over the manner of dividing the fifth (khumus) according to six opinions.

The first: A group said: The fifth is divided into six parts, and one sixth is set aside for the Ka'bah, which is what belongs to God; the second for the Messenger of God; the third for the kinsfolk (dhu al-qurba); the fourth for the orphans; the fifth for the needy; and the sixth for the wayfarer (ibn al-sabil).

The second opinion, held by Abu al-'Aliyah and al-Rabi': The spoils are divided into five parts. One part is set aside, and four parts are divided among those who took them. Then he puts his hand into the part he set aside, and whatever he takes from it he gives to the Ka'bah. Then he divides the remainder of the part he set aside into five: for the Messenger and those after him, according to the verse.

The third opinion: It is reported from Zayn al-'Abidin 'Ali ibn al-Husayn that he said: "The fifth belongs to us." It was said to him: "God says, ﴿and the orphans and the needy and the wayfarer﴾." He said: "Our orphans, our needy, and the sons of our wayfarers."

The fourth opinion, the view of al-Shafi'i: The fifth is divided into five parts. The share of God and the share of His Messenger are one share, spent on the interests of the believers. The four-fifths are for the four categories mentioned in the verse.

The fifth opinion, the view of Abu Hanifah: The fifth is divided into three: the orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer. The ruling concerning the kinship of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) ended with his death, just as the ruling concerning his share ended.

He said: From the fifth one begins with the repair of bridges, the building of mosques, and the provisions of judges and soldiers. Something similar to this is also reported from al-Shafi'i.

The sixth opinion, the view of Malik: It is left to the judgment and discretion of the imam, who takes from it without fixed measure, gives to the fighters from it according to his discretion, and spends the remainder on the interests of the Muslims.

Al-Qurtubi said: This is also the view of the four Caliphs, and they acted upon it. It is indicated by the saying of the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "I have nothing from what God has bestowed upon you as fay' except the fifth, and the fifth is returned to you." For he did not divide it into fifths or thirds. He only mentioned what is in the verse to draw attention to them, because they are among the most important of those to whom it is given.

Al-Zajjaj said, arguing for this opinion: God says, ﴿They ask you what they should spend. Say: Whatever good you spend is for the parents and the near relatives and the orphans and the needy and the wayfarer﴾ (al-Baqarah: 215). It is permissible by consensus to spend it on other than these categories if one sees fit.

His words, ﴿and for the near kinsfolk (dhi al-qurba)﴾: It has been said that repeating the preposition "li" before dhi al-qurba, but not before those after them, is to remove the assumption that they share in the Prophet's (ﷺ) share.

The scholars have differed concerning "al-qurba" (the near kin) according to several opinions. The first is that they are all of Quraysh. This was related from some of the early scholars, and it was used as evidence by the report that "the Prophet (ﷺ), when he ascended al-Safa, began calling out to all the clans of Quraysh, saying: 'O sons of so-and-so, O sons of so-and-so.'"

Al-Shafi'i, Ahmad, Abu Thawr, Mujahid, Qatadah, Ibn Jurayj, and Muslim ibn Khalid said: They are the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib, due to the saying of the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "The Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib are one thing," and he interlaced his fingers. It is in the Sahih. It was also said: They are the Banu Hashim alone. This was the view of Malik, al-Thawri, al-Awza'i and others, and it is related from 'Ali ibn al-Husayn and Mujahid.

His words, ﴿if you have believed in God﴾: al-Zajjaj said, from a group: The meaning is "Know that God is your Protector, if you have believed in God." Another group said: "in" is connected to His words, ﴿and know that whatever you acquire﴾. Ibn 'Atiyah said: This is the correct view, because His words "and know" contain a command to submit and accept the command of God regarding the spoils. So "in" (if) is linked to "and know" with this meaning: that is, if you are believers in God, then submit and accept God's command regarding the spoils, in what He has informed you of concerning the manner of dividing the spoils.

In al-Kashshaf it says: It is connected to an omitted element indicated by "and know", meaning: if you have believed in God, then know that the fifth of the spoils must be drawn near to God through, so cut off your desires concerning it, and be content with the four-fifths. The intended knowledge is not bare knowledge, but knowledge that includes action and obedience to God's command, because bare knowledge is equal for the believer and the disbeliever. End.

His words, ﴿and what We sent down upon Our servant﴾: It is conjoined to the divine name: that is, if you have believed in God and in what We sent down. ﴿The day of the Criterion﴾ is the day of Badr, because it distinguished between the people of truth and the people of falsehood. ﴿The two hosts﴾ are the two groups of Muslims and disbelievers. ﴿And God is over all things competent﴾. Among His great power is the victory of the smaller group over the larger.

His words, ﴿when you were on the near side of the valley and they were on the far side﴾: Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, and Ya'qub read "al-'udwah" with a kasra on the 'ayn in both places, and the rest read it with a damma. "Idh" is a substitute (badal) for ﴿the day of the Criterion﴾, and it is permissible for the governing element to be omitted: that is, remember when you were.

Al-'Udwah means the side of the valley. "Al-dunya" is the feminine of "al-adna" (nearer), and "al-quswa" is the feminine of "al-aqsa" (farther), from "dana yadna" and "qasa yaqsu". It is said "al-qusya" as well, and the original is with a waw. This is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz. The near side was the side toward Madinah, and the far side was the side toward Makkah.

The meaning: at the time of your encampment on the nearer side of the valley toward Madinah, and your enemy on its farther side, toward Makkah.

The clause ﴿and the caravan was lower than you﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal). The accusative of ﴿asfal﴾ is as an adverb of place (zarf), and its position is nominative as a predicate: that is, while the caravan was in a place lower than the place where you were.

Al-Akhfash, al-Kisa'i and al-Farra' permitted the nominative "asfalu" in the sense of "more low than you". "Al-rakb" is the plural of "rakib" (rider), and the Arabs do not say "rakb" except for a group of riders on camels. It is not said of one on a horse or other mounts. Ibn Faris said the same, and Ibn al-Sikkit related it from most of the lexicographers.

The meaning of "al-rakb" here is the caravan of Abu Sufyan, which is what is meant by "the caravan" (al-'ir), for they were in a place lower than them, toward the seashore.

It has been said: The benefit of mentioning this condition in which they were, being on the near side while their enemy was on the far side, with the caravan lower than them, is to indicate the strength of the enemy's position and power. This is because the far side where the polytheists camped had water in it and was land without any dry ground, while the near side was soft, where feet sank, with no water. The caravan was behind the enemy's back along with the enemy's great numbers. So God bestowed favour upon the Muslims by granting them victory over them in that condition.

His words, ﴿And if you had made a mutual appointment, you would have differed concerning the appointment﴾: That is, if you and the polytheists of Makkah had made a mutual appointment to meet at this place for battle, some of you would have disagreed with others. Your fewness and their great numbers would have deterred you from fulfilling the appointment, and what was in their hearts of awe of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) would have deterred them. But God brought you together in this encounter ﴿so that God might accomplish a matter that was [already] to be done﴾: that is, something deserving to be done by Him, namely the victory of His allies, the abasement of His enemies, the honouring of His religion, and the humbling of disbelief. He brought out the Muslims to seize the caravan and its spoils, in their own estimation, and brought out the disbelievers to defend it. It was not in the reckoning of either party that this encounter would take place in this manner. The "li" in ﴿li-yaqdiya﴾ is connected to an omitted element; the estimated meaning is: He gathered them in order that He might accomplish.

The clause ﴿that he who perished might perish by clear evidence and he who lived might live by clear evidence﴾ is a substitute (badal) for the clause before it: that is, so that whoever dies, dies upon clear evidence, and whoever lives, lives upon clear evidence, so that no one will have an argument against God. It has been said: "Perishing" and "living" are metaphors for disbelief and Islam, meaning that the Islam of whoever embraced Islam should proceed from clear evidence and certainty that it is the religion of truth, and the disbelief of whoever disbelieved should proceed from clear evidence and not from the intrusion of doubt.

Nafi', Khalaf, Sahl, Ya'qub, al-Bazzi, and Abu Bakr read "man hayya" with two yas, according to the original. The rest read with one ya, by assimilation (idgham). This is the choice of Abu 'Ubayd because it is written so in the Mushaf.

His words, ﴿and indeed God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾: that is, He hears the disbelief of the disbelievers and knows it, and He hears the faith of the believers and knows it.

Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Abbad ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: Then he set out the divisions of the fay' (spoils, here meaning the booty), and said: ﴿And know that whatever you gain as booty﴾ after what had already passed at Badr, ﴿then to Allah belongs one-fifth of it﴾, to the end of the verse.

Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and al-Hakim narrated from Qays ibn Muslim al-Jadali, who said: I asked al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, Ibn al-Hanafiyyah, about the words of Allah: ﴿And know that whatever you gain as booty, then to Allah belongs one-fifth of it﴾. He said: This is the key to the speech (miftah kalam, an introductory phrase that opens the sentence). ﴿To Allah belongs the world and the Hereafter﴾, ﴿and to the Messenger and to the near of kin﴾. After the death of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they disagreed about these two shares. One of them said: the share of the near of kin is for the kinsmen of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Another of them said: the share of the near of kin is for the kinsmen of the Caliph. Another of them said: the share of the Prophet (ﷺ) is for the Caliph after him. The opinion of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came together on making these two shares for horses and equipment in the way of Allah. That was in the caliphate of Abu Bakr and Umar.

Ibn Jarir, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent out a raiding party (sariyyah) and they gained booty, he would divide the booty into five and set aside that for his fifth," and then he recited: ﴿And know that whatever you gain...﴾ to the end of the verse. He said: His words ﴿then to Allah belongs one-fifth of it﴾ are the key to the speech: ﴿to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾. So Allah made the share of Allah and of the Messenger one share. ﴿And to the near of kin﴾: He made these two shares a strength for horses and weapons. And He made the share of orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer not to be given to anyone else. And He made the remaining four shares: one share for the horse, one share for its rider, and one share for the foot soldier.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him, who said: The booty was divided into five fifths. Four of them were among those who fought for it, and one fifth was divided into four parts: a quarter for Allah, for the Messenger, and for the near kin (dhu al-qurba), meaning the kinsmen of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Whatever was for Allah and the Messenger went to the kinsmen of the Prophet (ﷺ), and the Prophet (ﷺ) took nothing from the fifth. The second quarter was for the orphans, the third quarter (p-542) for the needy, and the fourth quarter for the wayfarer, who is the poor guest who stops among the Muslims.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Abu al-Aliyah concerning His words: ﴿And know that whatever you gain as booty﴾, to the end of the verse. He said: "The booty would be brought and placed down, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would divide it into five shares. He would set aside one share from it, and divide the four shares among the people, meaning among those who witnessed the battle. Then he would put his hand into the entire share he had set aside, and whatever he grasped from it he would give to the Kaʿbah. That is what Allah named: ﴿Do not assign to Allah a share, for to Allah belongs the world and the Hereafter.﴾ Then he would turn to the rest of that share and divide it into five parts: one share for the Prophet (ﷺ), one share for the near kin, one share for the orphans, one share for the needy, and one share for the wayfarer."

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) would set aside the share of Allah for the weapons, the horses, the way of Allah, the covering of the Kaʿbah, its perfume, and whatever the Kaʿbah needed. He would set aside the share of the Messenger for horses, weapons, and the maintenance of his household. The share of the near kin was for his kinsmen, which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would place among them together with their share among the people. For the orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer there were three shares, which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would place with whomever he wished, wherever he wished. The Banu Abd al-Muttalib have no part in these three shares, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had one share among the shares of the people."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Husayn al-Muʿallim, who said: I asked Abd Allah ibn Buraydah about the words: ﴿then to Allah belongs one-fifth of it, and to the Messenger﴾. He said: What belongs to Allah is for His Prophet, and what belongs to the Messenger is for his wives.

Al-Shafiʿi, Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Muslim, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated from Ibn Abbas that Najdah wrote to him asking him about the near kin whom Allah mentioned. He wrote back: "We used to see that they were us. But our people refused this for us, and said: all of Quraysh are near kin." The addition of his words "and they said: all of Quraysh are near kin" was transmitted by Abu Masharr alone, and in it there is weakness.

Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated by another route from Ibn Abbas that Najdah al-Haruri sent to him asking him about the share of the near kin, and saying: "To whom do you see it belonging?" Ibn Abbas said: It is for the kinsmen of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) allotted to them. Umar had proposed to us something of that, a proposal we saw as below our right, so we returned it to them and refused to accept it. He had offered them that he would help their unmarried men marry, that he would pay the debts of their indebted, and that he would give to their poor, but he refused to give them more than that.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: "I have spared you the washings of the hands, because for you in the fifth of the fifth there is what suffices you or makes you independent."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated this from Ibrahim ibn Mahdi al-Misisi, who said: al-Muʿtamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us from his father, from Hanash, from Ikrimah, from him, as a marfuʿ (traced to the Prophet ﷺ) report.

Ibn Kathir said: This is a hadith with a good chain (hasan al-isnad). Ibrahim ibn Mahdi was judged reliable by Abu Hatim, but Yahya ibn Maʿin said: He brings forth strange reports (manakir).

Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from al-Zuhri and Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, from Jubayr ibn Mutʿim: "The Prophet (ﷺ) divided the share of the near kin from Khaybar among the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib." He said: I and Uthman ibn Affan walked until we entered upon him, and we said: "O Messenger of Allah, these are your brothers from the Banu Hashim. We do not deny their merit because of your standing among them. But what about our brothers from the Banu al-Muttalib, whom you gave preference over us, when we and they are on the same level in lineage?" He said: "They have never separated from us, in the Jahiliyyah or in Islam."

Muslim has also narrated it in his Sahih.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: The family of Muhammad who were given the fifth are: the family of Ali, the family of al-Abbas, the family of Jafar, and the family of Aqil.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) had one item from the spoils which he would select for himself, either a servant or a horse. After that, he would take his share from the fifth.

Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ali, who said: "I said: O Messenger of Allah, would you not appoint me over what Allah has specified for us from the fifth? So he appointed me over it."

Al-Hakim narrated it and graded it sound (sahhahahu), from him, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) appointed me over the fifth of the fifth, and I placed it in its proper places during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and during the times of Abu Bakr and Umar."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas concerning His words: ﴿the Day of the Criterion (yawm al-furqan)﴾. He said: It is the Day of Badr, and Badr is between Makkah and Madinah.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim (who graded it sound), Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dalail narrated from Ibn Abbas concerning His words: ﴿the Day of the Criterion﴾. He said: It is the Day of Badr, on which Allah separated truth from falsehood.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: The Night of the Criterion was the night when the two hosts met. Its morning was the night of Friday, on the seventeenth day that had passed of Ramadan. Ibn Jarir also narrated it from him.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Abbas concerning His words: ﴿when you were on the nearer side of the valley (al-ʿudwah al-dunya)﴾. He said: "The nearer side of the valley is the edge of the wadi." ﴿And the caravan was lower than you﴾: he said, that was Abu Sufyan.

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ikrimah, who said: "The nearer side (al-ʿudwah al-dunya) is the nearer bank of the valley, and the farther side (al-ʿudwah al-quswa) is the farther bank of the valley."

Idh (إذْ) is in the accusative, governed by an implied verb: "remember" (اذْكُرْ). Alternatively, it is a second substitute (بَدَلٌ ثانٍ) for "the Day of the Criterion" (يَوْمِ الفُرْقانِ).

The meaning is that the Prophet (ﷺ) saw them in his dream as few, and he related that to his companions, and this was a cause of their steadfastness. Had he seen them in his dream as many, they would have faltered, lost heart about fighting them, and disputed over the matter, asking whether they should meet them or not. ﴿But God granted safety﴾: that is, He saved them and protected them from faltering and disputing, so He made them appear few in the eyes of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in the dream. It was also said that by "the dream" is meant the place of sleep, which is the eye, i.e., "in the place of your sleep, which is your eye." This was narrated from al-Hasan.

Al-Zajjaj said: "This view is good, but the first is more eloquent in Arabic (أسْوَغُ في العَرَبِيَّةِ), because of His saying: ﴿And when He showed them to you when you met, few in your eyes, and made you appear few in their eyes﴾." This indicates that this is the sight at the time of encounter, and that the other is the sight in sleep.

That is: "and remember the time when they were shown to you while they were few." [p. 543] This went so far that one Muslim said to another: "Do you think they are seventy?" He said: "They are about a hundred." The Muslims made the polytheists appear few in their eyes, until one of the latter said: "They are only the eaters of a camel-carcass." This was before the fighting. When they began the fighting, God made the Muslims appear numerous in the eyes of the polytheists, as He said in Al 'Imran: ﴿They see them as twice their number with the sight of the eye﴾ (3:13). The aspect of making the Muslims appear few in the eyes of the polytheists is that when they saw them as few, they advanced to fight without fear. Then they saw them as many, and they faltered, the circle turned against them, and the punishment of God and the lash of His retribution befell them.

It was repeated because the cause it expresses differs. ﴿And to God are all matters returned﴾: all of them. He does in them what He wills, and decrees in their affairs what He pleases.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ikrimah concerning the verse: he said, "Some of them urged others on."

Ibn Kathir said: "Its chain of transmission (isnad) is sound."

The lam in ﴿that God may accomplish a matter that was to be done﴾ is connected to an implied element, as a similar one occurred shortly before. It was repeated because the cause it expresses differs. ﴿And to God are all matters returned﴾: all of them. He does in them what He wills, and decrees in their affairs what He pleases.

Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Mujahid concerning His saying ﴿When God showed them to you in your dream as few﴾: He said, "God showed them to him in his dream as few, so the Prophet (ﷺ) informed his companions of that, and it was a source of reassurance for them."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah concerning His saying ﴿Had He shown them to you as many, you would have faltered﴾: he said, "You would have lost heart," ﴿and you would have disputed over the matter﴾: he said, "You would have differed."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿But God granted safety﴾: i.e., He completed (أتَمَّ).

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him, concerning ﴿But God granted safety﴾: he said, "He kept their affair secure for them until He made them victorious over their enemy."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, concerning His saying ﴿And when He showed them to you﴾ to the end of the verse: he said, "They appeared few in our eyes on the Day of Badr, until I said to a man beside me: 'Do you think they are seventy?' He said: 'No, they are a hundred.' Then we captured one of them and asked him, and he said: 'We were a thousand.'"

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ikrimah concerning the verse: he said, "Some of them urged others on."

Ibn Kathir said: "Its chain of transmission (isnad) is sound."

Ibn Ishaq narrated from Abbad ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr concerning His saying ﴿that God may accomplish a matter that was to be done﴾: i.e., that He might wind the war between them as retribution against whoever He wished to take vengeance upon, and as a blessing upon whoever among the people of His guardianship (wilayah) He wished to bestow blessing upon.

Idh (إذْ) is in the accusative, governed by an implied verb: "remember" (اذْكُرْ). Alternatively, it is a second substitute (بَدَلٌ ثانٍ) for "the Day of the Criterion" (يَوْمِ الفُرْقانِ).

The meaning is that the Prophet (ﷺ) saw them in his dream as few, and he related that to his companions, and this was a cause of their steadfastness. Had he seen them in his dream as many, they would have faltered, lost heart about fighting them, and disputed over the matter, asking whether they should meet them or not. ﴿But God granted safety﴾: that is, He saved them and protected them from faltering and disputing, so He made them appear few in the eyes of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in the dream. It was also said that by "the dream" is meant the place of sleep, which is the eye, i.e., "in the place of your sleep, which is your eye." This was narrated from al-Hasan.

Al-Zajjaj said: "This view is good, but the first is more eloquent in Arabic (أسْوَغُ في العَرَبِيَّةِ), because of His saying: ﴿And when He showed them to you when you met, few in your eyes, and made you appear few in their eyes﴾." This indicates that this is the sight at the time of encounter, and that the other is the sight in sleep.

As for His saying ﴿And when He showed them to you﴾ (وإذْ يُرِيكُمُوهُمْ): the temporal clause is in the accusative, governed by an implied verb coordinated with the first one. That is: "and remember the time when they were shown to you while they were few." [p. 543] This went so far that one Muslim said to another: "Do you think they are seventy?" He said: "They are about a hundred." The Muslims made the polytheists appear few in their eyes, until one of the latter said: "They are only the eaters of a camel-carcass." This was before the fighting. When they began the fighting, God made the Muslims appear numerous in the eyes of the polytheists, as He said in Al 'Imran: ﴿They see them as twice their number with the sight of the eye﴾ (3:13). The aspect of making the Muslims appear few in the eyes of the polytheists is that when they saw them as few, they advanced to fight without fear. Then they saw them as many, and they faltered, the circle turned against them, and the punishment of God and the lash of His retribution befell them.

It was repeated because the cause it expresses differs. ﴿And to God are all matters returned﴾: all of them. He does in them what He wills, and decrees in their affairs what He pleases.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him, concerning ﴿But God granted safety﴾: he said, "He kept their affair secure for them until He made them victorious over their enemy."

He said: 'No, they are a hundred.' Then we captured one of them and asked him, and he said: 'We were a thousand.'"

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ikrimah concerning the verse: he said, "Some of them urged others on."

Ibn Kathir said: "Its chain of transmission (isnad) is sound."

Ibn Ishaq narrated from Abbad ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr concerning His saying ﴿that God may accomplish a matter that was to be done﴾: i.e., that He might wind the war between them as retribution against whoever He wished to take vengeance upon, and as a blessing upon whoever among the people of His guardianship (wilayah) He wished to bestow blessing upon.

قَوْلُهُ: ﴿إذا لَقِيتُمْ فِئَةً﴾ اللِّقاءُ الحَرْبُ، والفِئَةُ الجَماعَةُ، أيْ إذا حارَبْتُمْ جَماعَةً مِنَ المُشْرِكِينَ فاثْبُتُوا لَهم ولا تَجْبُنُوا عَنْهم، وهَذا لا يُنافِي الرُّخْصَةَ المُتَقَدِّمَةَ في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿إلّا مُتَحَرِّفًا لِقِتالٍ أوْ مُتَحَيِّزًا إلى فِئَةٍ﴾ (الأنْفالِ: ١٦)، فَإنَّ الأمْرَ بِالثَّباتِ هو في حال السِّعَةِ، والرُّخْصَةُ هي في حالِ الضَّرُورَةِ.

وقَدْ لا يَحْصُلُ الثَّباتُ إلّا بِالتَّحَرُّفِ والتَّحَيُّزِ. ﴿واذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ﴾ أيِ اذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ عِنْدَ جَزَعِ قُلُوبِكم، فَإنَّ ذِكْرَهُ يُعِينُ عَلى الثَّباتِ في الشَّدائِدِ. وقِيلَ: المَعْنى: اثْبُتُوا بِقُلُوبِكم واذْكُرُوا بِألْسِنَتِكم، فَإنَّ القَلْبَ قَدْ يَسْكُنُ عِنْدَ اللِّقاءِ ويَضْطَرِبُ اللِّسانُ، فَأمَرَهم بِالذِّكْرِ حَتّى يَجْتَمِعَ ثَباتُ القَلْبِ واللِّسانِ. قِيلَ: ويَنْبَغِي أنْ يَكُونَ الذِّكْرُ في هَذِهِ الحالَةِ بِما قالَهُ أصْحابُ طالُوتَ: ﴿رَبَّنا أفْرِغْ عَلَيْنا صَبْرًا وثَبِّتْ أقْدامَنا وانْصُرْنا عَلى القَوْمِ الكافِرِينَ﴾ (البَقَرَةِ: ٢٥٠).

وفِي الآيَةِ دَلِيلٌ عَلى مَشْرُوعِيَّةِ الذِّكْرِ في جَمِيعِ الأحْوالِ، حَتّى في هَذِهِ الحالَةِ الَّتِي تَرْجُفُ فِيها القُلُوبُ وتَزِيغُ عِنْدَها البَصائِرُ.

ثُمَّ أمَرَهم بِطاعَةِ اللَّهِ فِيما يَأْمُرُهم بِهِ وطاعَةِ رَسُولِهِ فِيما يُرْشِدُهم إلَيْهِ، ونَهاهم عَنِ التَّنازُعِ وهو الِاخْتِلافُ في الرَّأْيِ، فَإنَّ ذَلِكَ يَتَسَبَّبُ عَنْهُ الفَشَلُ، وهو الجُبْنُ في الحَرْبِ.

والفاءُ جَوابُ النَّهْيِ، والفِعْلُ مَنصُوبٌ بِإضْمارِ "أنْ"، ويَجُوزُ أنْ يَكُونَ الفِعْلُ مَعْطُوفًا عَلى تَنازَعُوا مَجْزُومًا بِجازِمِهِ.

قَوْلُهُ: ﴿وتَذْهَبَ رِيحُكُمْ﴾ قُرِئَ بِنَصْبِ الفِعْلِ، وجَزْمِهِ عَطْفًا عَلى تَفْشَلُوا عَلى الوَجْهَيْنِ، والرِّيحُ: القُوَّةُ والنَّصْرُ، كَما يُقالُ: الرِّيحُ لِفُلانٍ إذا كانَ غالِبًا في الأمْرِ. وقِيلَ: الرِّيحُ الدَّوْلَةُ، شُبِّهَتْ في نُفُوذِ أمْرِها بِالرِّيحِ في هُبُوبِها، ومِنهُ قَوْلُ الشّاعِرِ:

إذا هَبَّتْ رِياحُكَ فاغْتَنَمَها ∗∗∗ فَعُقْبى كُلِّ خافِقَةٍ سُكُونُ

وقِيلَ: المُرادُ بِالرِّيحِ رِيحُ الصَّبا؛ لِأنَّ بِها كانَ يَنْصُرُ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ.

ثُمَّ أمَرَهم بِالصَّبْرِ عَلى شَدائِدِ الحَرْبِ، وأخْبَرَهم بِأنَّهُ مَعَ الصّابِرِينَ في كُلِّ أمْرٍ يَنْبَغِي الصَّبْرُ فِيهِ، ويا حَبَّذا هَذِهِ المَعِيَّةُ الَّتِي لا يَغْلِبُ مَن رُزِقَها غالِبٌ، ولا يُؤْتى صاحِبُها مِن جِهَةٍ مِنَ الجِهاتِ وإنْ كانَتْ كَثِيرَةً.

ثُمَّ نَهاهم عَنْ أنْ تَكُونَ حالَتُهم كَحالَةِ هَؤُلاءِ الَّذِينَ خَرَجُوا مِن دِيارِهِمْ بَطَرًا ورِئاءَ النّاسِ، وهم قُرَيْشٌ، فَإنَّهم خَرَجُوا يَوْمَ بَدْرٍ لِيَحْفَظُوا العِيرَ الَّتِي مَعَ أبِي سُفْيانَ، ومَعَهُمُ القِيانُ والمَعازِفُ، فَلَمّا بَلَغُوا الجُحْفَةَ بَلَغَهم أنَّ العِيرَ قَدْ نَجَتْ وسَلِمَتْ، فَلَمْ يَرْجِعُوا، بَلْ قالُوا: لا بُدَّ لَهم مِنَ الوُصُولِ إلى بَدْرٍ؛ لِيَشْرَبُوا الخَمْرَ، وتُغْنِيَ لَهُمُ القِيانُ، وتَسْمَعَ العَرَبُ بِمَخْرَجِهِمْ، فَكانَ ذَلِكَ مِنهم بَطَرًا وأشَرًا وطَلَبًا لِلثَّناءِ مِنَ النّاسِ، ولِلتَّمَدُّحِ إلَيْهِمْ والفَخْرِ عِنْدَهم، وهو الرِّياءُ. قِيلَ: والبَطَرُ في اللُّغَةِ: التَّقَوِّي بِنِعَمِ اللَّهِ عَلى مَعاصِيهِ، وهو مَصْدَرٌ في مَوْضِعِ الحالِ، أيْ خَرَجُوا بَطِرِينَ مُرائِينَ. وقِيلَ: هو مَفْعُولٌ لَهُ، وكَذا "رِياءً"، أيْ خَرَجُوا لِلْبَطَرِ والرِّياءِ.

وقَوْلُهُ: ﴿ويَصُدُّونَ﴾ مَعْطُوفٌ عَلى "بَطَرًا"، والمَعْنى كَما تَقَدَّمَ، أيْ خَرَجُوا بَطِرِينَ مُرائِينَ صادِّينَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ، أوْ لِلصَّدِّ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ، والصَّدُّ: إضْلالُ النّاسِ والحَيْلُولَةُ بَيْنَهم وبَيْنَ طُرُقِ الهِدايَةِ. ويَجُوزُ أنْ يَكُونَ ﴿ويَصُدُّونَ﴾ مَعْطُوفًا عَلى ﴿يَخْرُجُونَ﴾، والمَعْنى: يَجْمَعُونَ بَيْنَ الخُرُوجِ عَلى تِلْكَ الصِّفَةِ والصَّدِّ. ﴿واللَّهُ بِما يَعْمَلُونَ مُحِيطٌ﴾ لا تَخْفى عَلَيْهِ (p-٥٤٤) مِن أعْمالِهِمْ خافِيَةٌ، فَهو مُجازِيهِمْ عَلَيْها.

قَوْلُهُ: ﴿وإذْ زَيَّنَ لَهُمُ الشَّيْطانُ أعْمالَهُمْ﴾ الظَّرْفُ مُتَعَلِّقٌ بِمَحْذُوفٍ، أيْ واذْكُرْ يا مُحَمَّدُ وقْتَ تَزْيِينِ الشَّيْطانِ لَهم أعْمالَهم، والتَّزْيِينُ: التَّحْسِينُ. وقَدْ رُوِيَ أنَّ الشَّيْطانَ تَمَثَّلَ لَهم وقالَ لَهم تِلْكَ المَقالَةَ، وهي: ﴿لا غالِبَ لَكُمُ اليَوْمَ مِنَ النّاسِ وإنِّي جارٌ لَكم﴾، أيْ مُجِيرٌ لَكم مِن كُلِّ عَدُوٍّ، أوْ مِن بَنِي كِنانَةَ. ومَعْنى الجارِ هُنا: الدّافِعُ عَنْ صاحِبِهِ أنْواعَ الضَّرَرِ، كَما يَدْفَعُ الجارُ عَنِ الجارِ. وكانَ في صُورَةِ سُراقَةَ بْنِ مالِكِ بْنِ جَعْشَمٍ، وهو مِن بَنِي بَكْرِ بْنِ كِنانَةَ، وكانَتْ قُرَيْشٌ تَخافُ مِن بَنِي بَكْرٍ أنْ يَأْتُوهم مِن ورائِهِمْ. وقِيلَ: المَعْنى: إنَّهُ ألْقى في رُوعِهِمْ هَذِهِ المَقالَةَ، وخَيَّلَ إلَيْهِمْ أنَّهم لا يُغْلَبُونَ ولا يُطاقُونَ.

﴿فَلَمّا تَراءَتِ الفِئَتانِ﴾ أيْ فِئَةُ المُسْلِمِينَ والمُشْرِكِينَ ﴿نَكَصَ عَلى عَقِبَيْهِ﴾ أيْ رَجَعَ القَهْقَرى، ومِنهُ قَوْلُ الشّاعِرِ:

لَيْسَ النُّكُوصُ عَلى الأعْقابِ مُكْرُمَةً ∗∗∗ إنَّ المَكارِمَ إقْدامٌ عَلى الأمَلِ

وقَوْلُ الآخَرِ:

وما نَفَعَ المُسْتَأْخِرِينَ نُكُوصُهم ∗∗∗ ولا ضَرَّ أهْلَ السّابِقاتِ التَّقَدُّمُ

وقِيلَ: مَعْنى نَكَصَ هاهُنا: بَطَلَ كَيْدُهُ وذَهَبَ ما خَيَّلَهُ. ﴿وقالَ إنِّي بَرِيءٌ مِنكُمْ﴾ أيْ تَبَرَّأ مِنهم لَمّا رَأى أماراتِ النَّصْرِ مَعَ المُسْلِمِينَ بِإمْدادِ اللَّهِ لَهم بِالمَلائِكَةِ. ثُمَّ عَلَّلَ ذَلِكَ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿إنِّي أرى ما لا تَرَوْنَ﴾ يَعْنِي المَلائِكَةَ، ثُمَّ عَلَّلَ بِعِلَّةٍ أُخْرى فَقالَ: ﴿إنِّي أخافُ اللَّهَ﴾. قِيلَ: خافَ أنْ يُصابَ بِمَكْرُوهٍ مِنَ المَلائِكَةِ الَّذِينَ حَضَرُوا الوَقْعَةَ. وقِيلَ: إنَّ دَعْوى الخَوْفِ كَذِبٌ مِنهُ، ولَكِنَّهُ رَأى أنَّهُ لا قُوَّةَ لَهُ ولا لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ، فَاعْتَلَّ بِذَلِكَ. وجُمْلَةُ ﴿واللَّهُ شَدِيدُ العِقابِ﴾ يُحْتَمَلُ أنْ تَكُونَ مِن تَمامِ كَلامِ إبْلِيسَ، ويُحْتَمَلُ أنْ تَكُونَ كَلامًا مُسْتَأْنَفًا مِن جِهَةِ اللَّهِ سُبْحانَهُ.

قَوْلُهُ: ﴿إذْ يَقُولُ المُنافِقُونَ﴾ الظَّرْفُ مَعْمُولٌ لِفِعْلٍ مَحْذُوفٍ هو "اذْكُرْ"، ويَجُوزُ أنْ يَتَعَلَّقَ بِـ"نَكَصَ" أوْ بِـ"زَيَّنَ" أوْ بِـ"شَدِيدُ العِقابِ". قِيلَ: المُنافِقُونَ هُمُ الَّذِينَ أظْهَرُوا الإيمانَ وأبْطَنُوا الكُفْرَ. ﴿والَّذِينَ في قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ﴾ هُمُ الشّاكُّونَ مِن غَيْرِ نِفاقٍ، بَلْ لِكَوْنِهِمْ حَدِيثِي عَهْدٍ بِالإسْلامِ، فَوافَقُوا المُنافِقِينَ في قَوْلِهِمْ بِهَذِهِ المَقالَةِ، أعْنِي ﴿غَرَّ هَؤُلاءِ﴾ أيِ المُسْلِمِينَ ﴿دِينُهُمْ﴾ حَتّى تَكَلَّفُوا ما لا طاقَةَ لَهم بِهِ مِن قِتالِ قُرَيْشٍ. وقِيلَ: الَّذِينَ في قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ هُمُ المُشْرِكُونَ، ولا يَبْعُدُ أنْ يُرادَ بِهِمُ اليَهُودُ السّاكِنُونَ في المَدِينَةِ وما حَوْلَها، وأنَّهم هم والمُنافِقُونَ مِن أهْلِ المَدِينَةِ قالُوا هَذِهِ المَقالَةَ عِنْدَ خُرُوجِ المُسْلِمِينَ إلى بَدْرٍ، لَمّا رَأوْهم في قِلَّةٍ مِنَ العَدَدِ وضَعْفٍ مِنَ العُدَدِ. فَأجابَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿ومَن يَتَوَكَّلْ عَلى اللَّهِ فَإنَّ اللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ﴾ لا يَغْلِبُهُ غالِبٌ، ولا يُذِلُّ مَن تَوَكَّلَ عَلَيْهِ، ﴿حَكِيمٌ﴾ لَهُ الحِكْمَةُ البالِغَةُ الَّتِي تَقْصُرُ عِنْدَها العُقُولُ.

وقَدْ أخْرَجَ ابْنُ المُنْذِرِ، وابْنُ أبِي حاتِمٍ، وأبُو الشَّيْخِ، عَنْ قَتادَةَ في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿واذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ﴾ قالَ: افْتَرَضَ اللَّهُ ذِكْرَهُ عِنْدَ أشْغَلِ ما يَكُونُونَ: عِنْدَ الضِّرابِ بِالسُّيُوفِ.

وأخْرَجَ الحاكِمُ وصَحَّحَهُ، عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ سَعْدٍ قالَ: قالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: «ثِنْتانِ لا يُرَدّانِ: الدُّعاءُ عِنْدَ النِّداءِ، وعِنْدَ البَأْسِ حِينَ يُلْحِمُ بَعْضُهم بَعْضًا».

وأخْرَجَ الحاكِمُ وصَحَّحَهُ، عَنْ أبِي مُوسى: «أنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ كانَ يَكْرَهُ الصَّوْتَ عِنْدَ القِتالِ».

وأخْرَجَ ابْنُ المُنْذِرِ، وابْنُ أبِي حاتِمٍ، وأبُو الشَّيْخِ، عَنْ قَتادَةَ في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿ولا تَنازَعُوا فَتَفْشَلُوا وتَذْهَبَ رِيحُكم﴾ يَقُولُ: لا تَخْتَلِفُوا فَتَجْبُنُوا ويَذْهَبُ نَصْرُكم.

وأخْرَجَ الفِرْيابِيُّ، وابْنُ أبِي شَيْبَةَ، وابْنُ جَرِيرٍ، وابْنُ المُنْذِرِ، وابْنُ أبِي حاتِمٍ، وأبُو الشَّيْخِ، عَنْ مُجاهِدٍ في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿وتَذْهَبَ رِيحُكُمْ﴾ قالَ: نَصْرُكم، وقَدْ ذَهَبَ رِيحُ أصْحابِ مُحَمَّدٍ حِينَ نازَعُوهُ يَوْمَ أُحُدٍ.

وأخْرَجَ ابْنُ أبِي حاتِمٍ، وابْنُ مَرْدَوَيْهِ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ، في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿ولا تَكُونُوا كالَّذِينَ خَرَجُوا مِن دِيارِهِمْ﴾ الآيَةَ، يَعْنِي المُشْرِكِينَ الَّذِينَ قاتَلُوا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ يَوْمَ بَدْرٍ.

وأخْرَجَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ كَعْبٍ القُرَظِيِّ قالَ: لَمّا خَرَجَتْ قُرَيْشٌ مِن مَكَّةَ إلى بَدْرٍ خَرَجُوا بِالقِيانِ والدُّفُوفِ، فَأنْزَلَ اللَّهُ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ.

وأخْرَجَ ابْنُ أبِي شَيْبَةَ، وابْنُ المُنْذِرِ، عَنْ مُجاهِدٍ في الآيَةِ قالَ: أبُو جَهْلٍ وأصْحابُهُ يَوْمَ بَدْرٍ.

وأخْرَجَ ابْنُ المُنْذِرِ، وابْنُ أبِي حاتِمٍ، وأبُو الشَّيْخِ، عَنْ قَتادَةَ في الآيَةِ قالَ: «كانَ مُشْرِكُو قُرَيْشٍ الَّذِينَ قاتَلُوا نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ ﷺ يَوْمَ بَدْرٍ خَرَجُوا ولَهم بَغْيٌ وفَخْرٌ، وقَدْ قِيلَ لَهم يَوْمَئِذٍ: ارْجِعُوا فَقَدِ انْطَلَقَتْ عِيرُكم وقَدْ ظَفِرْتُمْ، فَقالُوا: لا واللَّهِ حَتّى يَتَحَدَّثَ أهْلُ الحِجازِ» بِمَسِيرِنا وعَدَدِنا. وذُكِرَ لَنا أنَّ نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ ﷺ قالَ يَوْمَئِذٍ: اللَّهُمَّ إنَّ قُرَيْشًا قَدْ أقْبَلَتْ بِفَخْرِها وخُيَلائِها لِتُجادِلَ رَسُولَكَ. وذُكِرَ لَنا أنَّهُ قالَ يَوْمَئِذٍ: «جاءَتْ مِن مَكَّةَ أفْلاذُها».

وأخْرَجَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ، وابْنُ المُنْذِرِ، وابْنُ أبِي حاتِمٍ، وابْنُ مَرْدَوَيْهِ، والبَيْهَقِيُّ في الدَّلائِلِ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ، قالَ: جاءَ إبْلِيسُ في جُنْدٍ مِنَ الشَّياطِينِ ومَعَهُ رايَةٌ في صُورَةِ رِجالٍ مِن بَنِي مُدْلِجٍ، والشَّيْطانُ في صُورَةِ سُراقَةَ بْنِ مالِكِ بْنِ جَعْشَمٍ، فَقالَ الشَّيْطانُ: ﴿لا غالِبَ لَكُمُ اليَوْمَ مِنَ النّاسِ وإنِّي جارٌ لَكم﴾. وأقْبَلَ جِبْرِيلُ عَلى إبْلِيسَ، فَلَمّا رَآهُ وكانَتْ يَدُهُ في يَدِ رَجُلٍ مِنَ المُشْرِكِينَ، انْتَزَعَ إبْلِيسُ يَدَهُ ووَلّى مُدْبِرًا وشِيعَتُهُ، فَقالَ الرَّجُلُ: يا سُراقَةُ إنَّكَ جارٌ لَنا! فَقالَ: ﴿إنِّي أرى ما لا تَرَوْنَ﴾ وذَلِكَ حِينَ رَأى المَلائِكَةَ ﴿إنِّي أخافُ اللَّهَ واللَّهُ شَدِيدُ العِقابِ﴾. قالَ: ولَمّا دَنا القَوْمُ بَعْضُهم مِن بَعْضٍ قَلَّلَ اللَّهُ المُسْلِمِينَ في أعْيُنِ المُشْرِكِينَ، وقَلَّلَ المُشْرِكِينَ في أعْيُنِ المُسْلِمِينَ، فَقالَ المُشْرِكُونَ: ﴿وما هَؤُلاءِ غَرَّ هَؤُلاءِ دِينُهم﴾، وإنَّما قالُوا ذَلِكَ مِن قِلَّتِهِمْ في أعْيُنِهِمْ، وظَنُّوا أنَّهم سَيَهْزِمُونَهم لا يَشُكُّونَ في ذَلِكَ، فَقالَ اللَّهُ: ﴿ومَن يَتَوَكَّلْ عَلى اللَّهِ فَإنَّ اللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ﴾.

وأخْرَجَ الطَّبَرانِيُّ، وأبُو نُعَيْمٍ، عَنْ رِفاعَةَ بْنِ رافِعٍ الأنْصارِيِّ قالَ: لَمّا رَأى إبْلِيسُ ما تَفْعَلُ المَلائِكَةُ بِالمُشْرِكِينَ يَوْمَ بَدْرٍ أشْفَقَ أنْ يَخْلُصَ القَتْلُ إلَيْهِ، فَتَشَبَّثَ بِهِ الحارِثُ بْنُ هاشِمٍ وهو يَظُنُّ أنَّهُ سُراقَةُ بْنُ مالِكٍ، فَوَكَزَ في صَدْرِ الحارِثِ فَألْقاهُ، ثُمَّ خَرَجَ هارِبًا حَتّى ألْقى نَفْسَهُ في البَحْرِ، ورَفَعَ يَدَيْهِ فَقالَ: اللَّهُمَّ إنِّي أسْألُكَ نَظِرَتَكَ إيّايَ.

وأخْرَجَ الواقِدِيُّ، وابْنُ مَرْدَوَيْهِ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ، نَحْوَهُ.

وأخْرَجَ ابْنُ أبِي حاتِمٍ، وأبُو الشَّيْخِ، عَنْ قَتادَةَ في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿إنِّي أرى ما لا تَرَوْنَ﴾ قالَ: ذُكِرَ لَنا أنَّهُ رَأى جِبْرِيلَ تَنْزِلُ مَعَهُ المَلائِكَةُ، فَعَلِمَ عَدُوُّ اللَّهِ أنَّهُ لا يَدانِ لَهُ بِالمَلائِكَةِ، وقالَ: ﴿إنِّي أخافُ اللَّهَ﴾ كَذِبَ عَدُوُّ اللَّهِ، ما بِهِ (p-٥٤٥) مَخافَةُ اللَّهِ، ولَكِنْ عَلِمَ أنَّهُ لا قُوَّةَ لَهُ بِهِ ولا مَنَعَةَ لَهُ.

وأخْرَجَ عَبْدُ الرَّزّاقِ، وابْنُ المُنْذِرِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ قالَ: ذَكَرُوا أنَّهم أقْبَلُوا عَلى سُراقَةَ بْنِ مالِكٍ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ، فَأنْكَرَ أنْ يَكُونَ قالَ شَيْئًا مِن ذَلِكَ.

وأخْرَجَ ابْنُ أبِي حاتِمٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ، في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿إذْ يَقُولُ المُنافِقُونَ﴾ قالَ: وهم يَوْمَئِذٍ في المُسْلِمِينَ.

وأخْرَجَ عَبْدُ الرَّزّاقِ، وابْنُ المُنْذِرِ، وابْنُ أبِي حاتِمٍ، عَنِ الحَسَنِ في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿والَّذِينَ في قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ﴾ قالَ: هم قَوْمٌ لَمْ يَشْهَدُوا القِتالَ يَوْمَ بَدْرٍ فَسُمُّوا مُنافِقِينَ.

وأخْرَجَ عَبْدُ الرَّزّاقِ، وابْنُ المُنْذِرِ، عَنِ الكَلْبِيِّ، في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿والَّذِينَ في قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ﴾ قالَ: هم قَوْمٌ كانُوا أقَرُّوا بِالإسْلامِ وهم بِمَكَّةَ، ثُمَّ خَرَجُوا مَعَ المُشْرِكِينَ يَوْمَ بَدْرٍ، فَلَمّا رَأوُا المُسْلِمِينَ قالُوا: ﴿غَرَّ هَؤُلاءِ دِينُهم﴾.

وأخْرَجَ ابْنُ المُنْذِرِ، وأبُو الشَّيْخِ، عَنِ الشَّعْبِيِّ، نَحْوَهُ.

His saying: ﴿And if you could see﴾. The address is to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), or to everyone who is fit to be addressed, as its verification has been explained earlier in more than one place. The meaning is "if you had seen," because *law* (لَوْ, "if"; a conditional particle) turns the present tense into the past. *Idh* (إذْ, "when") is an adverb of time governing *tará* (تَرى, "you see"), and its object is omitted. That is: "if you could see the disbelievers at the time the angels take their souls." It has been said that by "those who disbelieved" he means those who were not killed on the day of Badr. It has also been said that it refers to those who were killed at Badr. The answer to *law* is omitted, and its estimated form is "you would see a terrible thing." The clause ﴿they strike their faces﴾ is in a position of accusative as a circumstantial clause (*hal*, "state"). By ﴿their backs﴾ (أدبارهم) is meant their buttocks (أسْتاههم); it is a euphemism expressed by "backs." It has also been said that it means their backs. It has been said that this striking happens at the time of death, as the mention of "taking the souls" indicates. It has also been said that it happens on the Day of Resurrection, when they are driven toward the Fire.

His saying: ﴿And taste the punishment of the burning﴾. This was said by al-Farra' (the grammarian). The meaning is: "and they say, 'Taste the punishment of the burning.'" The clause is conjoined to *yadribūna* (يَضْرِبُونَ, "they strike"). It has been said that the Keepers of Hell (خَزَنَة جَهَنَّمَ) say this statement to them. *Dhawq* (الذَّوْق, "tasting") may be perceptible, and it may also be used in the place of trial and testing; its origin is tasting with the mouth.

The demonstrative in His saying ﴿that﴾ refers to what preceded of striking and punishment. The *bāʾ* (بِ, "because of") in ﴿because of what your hands have sent forward﴾ is causal: that is, this occurs because of what you have earned of sins and committed of wrongdoings. The clause ﴿and that Allah is not unjust to the servants﴾ is in a position of nominative, as the predicate of an omitted subject: "and the matter is that He does not wrong them." It is also permissible that it be conjoined to the clause which is the predicate of His saying ﴿that﴾, namely ﴿because of what your hands have sent forward﴾. That is: "that punishment is because of the sins, and because of ﴿that Allah is not unjust to the servants﴾," since He, glory be to Him, sent His messengers to them, sent down His books upon them, made the path clear to them, and guided them to the two highways, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And We did not wrong them, but they were wronging themselves﴾ (An-Nahl: 118).

His saying: ﴿Like the habit of the people of Pharaoh﴾. When Allah, glory be to Him, mentioned what He had sent down upon the people of Badr, He followed it with what indicates that this is His way with the groups of disbelievers. *Da'b* (الدَّأْب, "habit, custom") means custom. The *kāf* (كَ, "like") is in a position of nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject: that is, "the habit of these is like the habit of the people of Pharaoh ﴿and those before them﴾."

The meaning is that these were requited as those were requited, so the custom of the punishment of these was like the past custom of Allah in punishing groups of disbelief. The clause ﴿they disbelieved in the signs of Allah﴾ explains the *da'b* of the people of Pharaoh: that is, their habit is this, that they disbelieved in the signs of Allah, so Allah's seizing them resulted from their disbelief. By ﴿their sins﴾ is meant their disobediences that follow from their disbelief.
