The *bāʾ* (بِ, "because of") in ﴿because of what your hands have sent forward﴾ is causal: that is, this occurs because of what you have earned of sins and committed of wrongdoings. The clause ﴿and that Allah is not unjust to the servants﴾ is in a position of nominative, as the predicate of an omitted subject: "and the matter is that He does not wrong them." It is also permissible that it be conjoined to the clause which is the predicate of His saying ﴿that﴾, namely ﴿because of what your hands have sent forward﴾. That is: "that punishment is because of the sins, and because of ﴿that Allah is not unjust to the servants﴾," since He, glory be to Him, sent His messengers to them, sent down His books upon them, made the path clear to them, and guided them to the two highways, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And We did not wrong them, but they were wronging themselves﴾ (An-Nahl: 118).

His saying: ﴿Like the habit of the people of Pharaoh﴾. When Allah, glory be to Him, mentioned what He had sent down upon the people of Badr, He followed it with what indicates that this is His way with the groups of disbelievers. *Da'b* (الدَّأْب, "habit, custom") means custom. The *kāf* (كَ, "like") is in a position of nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject: that is, "the habit of these is like the habit of the people of Pharaoh ﴿and those before them﴾."

The meaning is that these were requited as those were requited, so the custom of the punishment of these was like the past custom of Allah in punishing groups of disbelief. The clause ﴿they disbelieved in the signs of Allah﴾ explains the *da'b* of the people of Pharaoh: that is, their habit is this, that they disbelieved in the signs of Allah, so Allah's seizing them resulted from their disbelief. By ﴿their sins﴾ is meant their disobediences that follow from their disbelief. Thus the *bāʾ* in ﴿because of their sins﴾ is of association (لِلْمُلابَسَة): that is, He seized them while they were involved in their sins, not repenting from them. The clause ﴿Indeed Allah is Strong and severe in punishment﴾ is a parenthetical clause confirming what precedes it.

The demonstrative in His saying ﴿that﴾ refers to the punishment which Allah sent upon them. It is a subject whose predicate is what follows it, and the clause functions as a reason for what befell them of the punishment of Allah.

The meaning is: that punishment is because Allah's custom with His servants is that He does not change the blessings which He bestows upon them, ﴿until they change what is in themselves﴾ of states and character, by denying the blessings of Allah, disregarding His favour, and neglecting His commands and prohibitions. This is as it was with the people of Pharaoh and those before them, and with the Quraysh and those who resemble them among the polytheists. Allah opened for them the doors of good in this world and favoured them by sending messengers and sending down books, but they met these blessings with disbelief, so they deserved the change of the blessings, just as they changed what it was obligatory for them to follow and act upon of gratitude for them and acceptance of them. The clause ﴿and that Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾ is conjoined to ﴿because Allah did not change a blessing﴾ and is included with it in the reason: that is, "that is because Allah did not change...," and because Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing, who hears what they say and knows what they do.

It has been recited with a *kasra* on the hamza (إنَّ, "indeed") as a resumptive start (لِلِاسْتِئْنَاف).

Then He repeated what had preceded, saying: ﴿Like the habit of the people of Pharaoh and those before them; they denied the signs of their Lord﴾, for the purpose of emphasis, with the added point that it serves as an explanation of the seizing for their sins, that it was by drowning. It has been said that the first refers to what the people of Pharaoh and those likened to them did, and the second refers to what was done to them. It has also been said that the first means their disbelief in Allah and the second means their denial of the prophets. It has been said that other than this, which is not free from strained interpretation. The discourse about ﴿We destroyed them for their sins﴾ is like the earlier discourse on ﴿So Allah seized them for their sins﴾. ﴿And We drowned the people of Pharaoh﴾ is conjoined to "We destroyed them," as the conjunction of the specific to the general, because of its severity and because it is one of the most severe kinds of destruction. Then He judged both groups, the people of Pharaoh and those before them, and the disbelieving Quraysh, as having wronged themselves by what they brought upon themselves of the punishment of Allah through disbelief in Allah, His signs and His messengers, and by wronging others, as used to occur from them in their dealings with people through various kinds of injustice.

Ibn Abi Hatim has transmitted, from al-Dahhak, regarding His saying ﴿When the angels take the souls of those who disbelieved﴾, that he said: those whom Allah killed at Badr from among the polytheists.

Ibn Jarir has transmitted, from al-Hasan, who said: A man said, "O Messenger of Allah, I saw on the back of Abu Jahl something like thorns." He said: "That is the striking of the angels." This is a mursal report.

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh have transmitted, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿and their backs﴾, that he said: their buttocks, but Allah is Generous and uses euphemism.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh have transmitted, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying ﴿That is because Allah did not change a blessing He had bestowed upon a people until they change what is in themselves﴾, that he said: The blessing of Allah is Muhammad (ﷺ), whom Allah bestowed upon the Quraysh, but they disbelieved, so Allah transferred him to the Ansar.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 8, verses 55–60:

His saying: ﴿Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah﴾ means the worst of what crawls upon the face of the earth. ﴿In the sight of Allah﴾ means in His judgment. ﴿Are those who disbelieve﴾ means those who persist in disbelief and persevere in misguidance. Therefore He said: ﴿so they will not believe﴾, meaning: this is their condition, they will never believe, and they will not return from error at all. He made them the worst of living creatures, not the worst of people, as an indication of their having stripped away humanity and entered a category other than people, among the kinds of animals, because they do not use their reason for that which would guide them.

His saying: ﴿with whom you made a treaty﴾ is a substitution (badal) for ﴿those who disbelieve﴾, or an explicative apposition (ʿatf bayan), or in the accusative position by way of censure (al-dhamm).

The meaning: These disbelievers who are the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are those with whom you made a treaty, that is, you took their covenant. Then they ﴿break their covenant﴾ which you made ﴿every time﴾ of the occasions of the treaty, while they ﴿do not fear﴾ breaking it, do not dread its consequence, and do not avoid its causes. It is said that the "min" in His saying "minhum" (from among them) is partitive (lil-tabʿid), and the object of ʿahadta (you made a treaty) is omitted, meaning: those with whom you made a treaty, and they are some of those disbelievers, namely their nobles. He conjoined the future tense, "then they break," to the past tense "you made a treaty," to indicate the continuity of their breaking [of the covenant]. These are the Banu Qurayzah, with whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made a treaty that they would not assist the disbelievers, but they did not fulfill that, as will come.

Then Allah commanded the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to be severe and harsh towards them, saying: ﴿So if you overpower them in war, then disperse those behind them with them﴾, meaning: if you encounter them in a situation where you are able over them and can overcome them, ﴿then disperse those behind them﴾, meaning: scatter by killing them, and by punishing them, those behind them of the warring ones, from the people of polytheism, so that they fear your side and refrain from fighting you, for fear that what befell these people will befall them.

The word al-thiqaf in the original language is that with which a spear or the like is bound. From it is the saying of al-Nabighah:
"She calls Quʿayb, while the iron has choked on her, choked as the thiqaf chokes on the joining of the reeds."
It is said: thaqiftuhu, meaning I found him; and fulan thaqif means one who is quick to find what he seeks. Al-tashrid is scattering together with agitation.

Abu ʿUbayda said: ﴿fa-sharrid bihim﴾ means "sammiʿ bihim" (make an example of them).

Al-Zajjaj said: Do an act of killing with them by which you scatter those behind them. It is said: "sharradtu Banu Fulan," meaning: I uprooted them from their places and drove them away from them until they departed from them.

The poet said:
"I wander through the valleys every day, fearing that the Wise One will scatter me."

From this is the saying: "sharada al-baʿir" (the camel bolted), when it departed from its owner. It is narrated from Ibn Masʿud that he recited "fa-sharridh bihim" with the dotted dhal.

Qutrub said: al-tashrid with the dotted dhal is al-tankil (exemplary punishment), and with the undotted (dal) it is scattering.

Al-Mahdawi said: The dotted dhal has no basis except that it is a replacement for the undotted dal due to their proximity. He said: "fa-sharrid" is not known in the language. And it was read "min khalfihim" with a kasra on the mim and the fa.

His saying: ﴿And if you fear treachery from a people﴾ means deceit and breaking of the covenant from the treaty-making people. ﴿Then throw back to them﴾ means cast to them the covenant that is between you and them ﴿on equal terms﴾, on a level path.

The meaning: he informs them openly and plainly of the breach, and does not attack them by surprise in war. It is said: the meaning of "on equal terms" is in a manner whereby the knowledge of the breach is equal for the farthest and nearest of them, or that you and they are equal in it. Al-Kisaʾi said: al-sawaʾ means justice, and it may also mean the middle. From it is His saying: ﴿in the midst of the blazing fire﴾ (al-Saffat: 55). From it is the saying of Hassan:
"Woe to the helpers of the Prophet and his kin, after the disappearance in the midst of the grave of the atheist."
And from the first meaning is the saying of the poet:
"Strike the faces of the treacherous enemies until they come to terms (sawaʾ)."
It is said: the meaning of ﴿throw back to them on equal terms﴾ is openly and not secretly. The apparent view is that this verse is general for every treaty-partner from whom breaking the covenant is feared.

Ibn ʿAtiyyah said: What appears from the wording of the Qur'an is that the matter of the Banu Qurayzah ended at His saying ﴿so disperse those behind them with them﴾, then He, blessed and exalted, began in this verse commanding him regarding what he should do in the future with whomever he fears treachery from. The clause ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love the treacherous﴾ is a reason for what precedes it. It may be a warning to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) against engaging in battle before he throws back to them on equal terms, and it may refer to the people from whom treachery is feared.

His saying: "Wa-la tahsabanna" (And let them not think). Ibn ʿAmir, Yazid and Hafs read it with the yaʾ (third person), and the rest read it with the taʾ (second person).

According to the first reading, "those who disbelieve" is the subject of the verb of thinking, and its first object is omitted, meaning: let not those who disbelieve think themselves [to have] outstripped; and its second object is "sabaqu" (outstripped), meaning: they escaped and got away from being overtaken.

According to the second reading, the address is to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), its first object is "those who disbelieve," and the second is "sabaqu." It was also read "innahum sabaqu," and it was read "yahsibanna" with a kasra on the sin. The clause ﴿Indeed they cannot escape﴾ is a reason for what precedes it, meaning: they will not get away, and their pursuer will not find himself incapable of overtaking them.

Ibn ʿAmir read "annahum" with a fatha on the hamza, and the rest with a kasra. Both readings make the clause explanatory (taʿlilliyyah). It was said: what is intended by this verse is whoever escaped from the Battle of Badr among the polytheists.

The meaning: even if they escaped from this event and were saved, they will not escape, but rather they will be subject to the punishment of Allah in this world or in the Hereafter.

A group of grammarians, among them Abu Hatim, claimed that the reading of whoever read "yahsabanna" with the yaʾ is a grave error, and that it is not permissible to recite it so, because "yahsabanna" does not come with only one object, while it requires two objects.

Al-Nahhas said: This is a severe overreach. The meaning of this reading is: let not those behind them who disbelieve think they outstripped, so the pronoun refers to what came before. However, the reading with the taʾ is clearer.

Al-Mahdawi said: According to this reading it is permissible for "those who disbelieve" to be the subject, with the first object omitted. The meaning: let not those who disbelieve think themselves to have outstripped.

Makki said: It is also permissible that "an" be implied with "sabaqu," so that it stands in place of the two objects, and the estimate is: let not those who disbelieve think that they outstripped. This is like His saying ﴿Do people think that they will be left alone?﴾ (al-ʿAnkabut: 2), in that "an" stands in place of the two objects.

Then He, glorified be He, commanded the preparation of strength against the enemies. Strength is everything by which one is empowered in war, and among that are weapons and bows.

It is established in Sahih Muslim and others, from the hadith of ʿUqbah ibn ʿAmir, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was on the minbar saying: "﴿And prepare against them whatever you are able of strength﴾. Indeed, strength is archery. He said it three times."

It was said: it refers to fortresses, but returning to the authentic explanation from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is the necessary course.

His saying: ﴿and of steeds of war﴾. Al-Hasan, ʿAmr ibn Dinar and Abu Haywah read "wa-min rubuṭ al-khayl" with a damma on the ra' and the ba', like kutub, the plural of kitab.

Abu Hatim said: ribat of horses is five or more, which are the horses tethered facing the enemy. From it is the saying of the poet:
"God commanded their tethering against His enemy in war; indeed God is the best granter of success."

In al-Kashshaf: al-ribat is a name for the horses that are tethered in the way of Allah. It may also be called ribat, which means garrisoning, and it may be the plural of rabit, like fasil and fisal. End.

Whoever interprets strength as everything by which one is strengthened in war makes the conjunction of horses a conjunction of the specific over the general. The clause ﴿by which you will terrify the enemy of Allah and your enemy﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal). Al-tarhib is intimidation. The pronoun in "bihi" refers either to "ma" in "ma istatatum" or to the verbal noun implied by ﴿and prepare﴾, which is preparation.

The enemies of Allah and your enemies are the polytheists of Mecca and others from the polytheist Arabs.

His saying: ﴿and others besides them﴾ is conjoined to "enemy of Allah and your enemy". The meaning of "besides them" is "other than them." It is said: they are the Jews. It is said: Persia and Rome. It is said: the jinn, and Ibn Jarir preferred this. It is said: by "others" is meant everyone whose enmity is not known, as stated by al-Suhayli. It is said: they are the Banu Qurayzah specifically. It is said: other than that. The better course is to suspend judgment on their identification, due to His saying: ﴿You do not know them; Allah knows them﴾.

His saying: ﴿And whatever you spend in the way of Allah﴾, meaning in jihad, even if it is little, in truth, ﴿will be repaid to you﴾, its reward in the Hereafter. So a good deed is multiplied tenfold up to seven hundred times, and up to many multiples, as we established earlier. ﴿And you will not be wronged﴾ in any part of this expenditure which you spend in the way of Allah, meaning in its reward; rather it will come to you full, abundant and complete: ﴿And if it is a good deed, He doubles it and gives from Himself a great reward﴾ (al-Nisa': 40), ﴿Indeed I do not waste the work of any worker among you﴾ (Al ʿImran: 195).

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, who said: The verse ﴿Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah﴾ and what follows was revealed concerning six men of the Jews, among them Ibn Tabut.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿those with whom you made a treaty, then they break their covenant﴾, that he said: Qurayzah on the day of the Trench assisted the enemies of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) against him.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying: ﴿so disperse those behind them with them﴾, that he said: make an example of those behind them after them.

Ibn Jarir narrated from him concerning the verse, that he said: make an example of those behind them.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Saʿid ibn Jubayr concerning the verse, that he said: warn by them.

ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah, that he said: admonish by them those others among the people.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Zayd, that he said: frighten them by them.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from al-Suddi, concerning His saying: ﴿that they may remember﴾, they say: that they may take heed lest they break [their oaths] and the same be done to them.

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Shihab, who said: "Jibril entered upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'You have laid down the weapons, and we have not ceased pursuing the people. So go out, for Allah has permitted you against Qurayzah, and revealed concerning them: ﴿And if you fear treachery from a people﴾ and the verse.'"

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying: ﴿Indeed they cannot escape﴾, that he said: they will not get away from us.

Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying: ﴿And prepare against them whatever you are able of strength﴾, that he said: archery, swords and weapons.

Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from ʿAbbad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr concerning His saying: ﴿And prepare against them whatever you are able of strength﴾, that he said: He commanded them to prepare horses.

Abu al-Shaykh and al-Bayhaqi in Shuʿab al-Iman narrated from ʿIkrimah concerning the verse, that he said: strength is male horses, and ribat is females.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated similarly from Mujahid.

Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab concerning the verse, that he said: strength is the horse, up to the arrow and what is below it.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from ʿIkrimah, that he said: strength is fortresses, and ﴿of steeds of war﴾ is females.

al-Firyabi, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying: ﴿by which you will terrify the enemy of Allah and your enemy﴾, that he said: you will disgrace by it the enemy of Allah and your enemy.

Numerous hadiths have come concerning the recommendation of archery and the reward in it.

Likewise, hadiths have come concerning the recommendation of keeping horses and preparing them, and the great reward of their owner, which the scope of this discussion does not allow to be expanded upon.

A group of scholars have devoted separate works to this subject.

The clause ﴿Indeed they cannot escape﴾ is a reason for what precedes it, meaning: they will not get away, and their pursuer will not find himself incapable of overtaking them.

Ibn ʿAmir read "annahum" with a fatha on the hamza, and the rest with a kasra. Both readings make the clause explanatory (taʿlilliyyah). It was said: what is intended by this verse is whoever escaped from the Battle of Badr among the polytheists.

The meaning: even if they escaped from this event and were saved, they will not escape, but rather they will be subject to the punishment of Allah in this world or in the Hereafter.

A group of grammarians, among them Abu Hatim, claimed that the reading of whoever read "yahsabanna" with the yaʾ is a grave error, and that it is not permissible to recite it so, because "yahsabanna" does not come with only one object, while it requires two objects.

Al-Nahhas said: This is a severe overreach. The meaning of this reading is: let not those behind them who disbelieve think they outstripped, so the pronoun refers to what came before. However, the reading with the taʾ is clearer.

Al-Mahdawi said: According to this reading it is permissible for "those who disbelieve" to be the subject, with the first object omitted. The meaning: let not those who disbelieve think themselves to have outstripped.

Makki said: It is also permissible that "an" be implied with "sabaqu," so that it stands in place of the two objects, and the estimate is: let not those who disbelieve think that they outstripped. This is like His saying ﴿Do people think that they will be left alone?﴾ (al-ʿAnkabut: 2), in that "an" stands in place of the two objects.

Then He, glorified be He, commanded the preparation of strength against the enemies. Strength is everything by which one is empowered in war, and among that are weapons and bows.

It is established in Sahih Muslim and others, from the hadith of ʿUqbah ibn ʿAmir, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was on the minbar saying: "﴿And prepare against them whatever you are able of strength﴾. Indeed, strength is archery. He said it three times."

It was said: it refers to fortresses, but returning to the authentic explanation from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is the necessary course.

His saying: ﴿and of steeds of war﴾. Al-Hasan, ʿAmr ibn Dinar and Abu Haywah read "wa-min rubuṭ al-khayl" with a damma on the ra' and the ba', like kutub, the plural of kitab.

Abu Hatim said: ribat of horses is five or more, which are the horses tethered facing the enemy. From it is the saying of the poet:
"God commanded their tethering against His enemy in war; indeed God is the best granter of success."

In al-Kashshaf: al-ribat is a name for the horses that are tethered in the way of Allah. It may also be called ribat, which means garrisoning, and it may be the plural of rabit, like fasil and fisal. End.

Whoever interprets strength as everything by which one is strengthened in war makes the conjunction of horses a conjunction of the specific over the general. The clause ﴿by which you will terrify the enemy of Allah and your enemy﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal). Al-tarhib is intimidation. The pronoun in "bihi" refers either to "ma" in "ma istatatum" or to the verbal noun implied by ﴿and prepare﴾, which is preparation.

The enemies of Allah and your enemies are the polytheists of Mecca and others from the polytheist Arabs.

His saying: ﴿and others besides them﴾ is conjoined to "enemy of Allah and your enemy". The meaning of "besides them" is "other than them." It is said: they are the Jews. It is said: Persia and Rome. It is said: the jinn, and Ibn Jarir preferred this. It is said: by "others" is meant everyone whose enmity is not known, as stated by al-Suhayli. It is said: they are the Banu Qurayzah specifically. It is said: other than that. The better course is to suspend judgment on their identification, due to His saying: ﴿You do not know them; Allah knows them﴾.

His saying: ﴿And whatever you spend in the way of Allah﴾, meaning in jihad, even if it is little, in truth, ﴿will be repaid to you﴾, its reward in the Hereafter. So a good deed is multiplied tenfold up to seven hundred times, and up to many multiples, as we established earlier. ﴿And you will not be wronged﴾ in any part of this expenditure which you spend in the way of Allah, meaning in its reward; rather it will come to you full, abundant and complete: ﴿And if it is a good deed, He doubles it and gives from Himself a great reward﴾ (al-Nisa': 40), ﴿Indeed I do not waste the work of any worker among you﴾ (Al ʿImran: 195).

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, who said: The verse ﴿Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah﴾ and what follows was revealed concerning six men of the Jews, among them Ibn Tabut.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿those with whom you made a treaty, then they break their covenant﴾, that he said: Qurayzah on the day of the Trench assisted the enemies of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) against him.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying: ﴿so disperse those behind them with them﴾, that he said: make an example of those behind them after them.

Ibn Jarir narrated from him concerning the verse, that he said: make an example of those behind them.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Saʿid ibn Jubayr concerning the verse, that he said: warn by them.

ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah, that he said: admonish by them those others among the people.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Zayd, that he said: frighten them by them.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from al-Suddi, concerning His saying: ﴿that they may remember﴾, they say: that they may take heed lest they break [their oaths] and the same be done to them.

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Shihab, who said: "Jibril entered upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'You have laid down the weapons, and we have not ceased pursuing the people. So go out, for Allah has permitted you against Qurayzah, and revealed concerning them: ﴿And if you fear treachery from a people﴾ and the verse.'"

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying: ﴿Indeed they cannot escape﴾, that he said: they will not get away from us.

Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying: ﴿And prepare against them whatever you are able of strength﴾, that he said: archery, swords and weapons.

Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from ʿAbbad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr concerning His saying: ﴿And prepare against them whatever you are able of strength﴾, that he said: He commanded them to prepare horses.

Abu al-Shaykh and al-Bayhaqi in Shuʿab al-Iman narrated from ʿIkrimah concerning the verse, that he said: strength is male horses, and ribat is females.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated similarly from Mujahid.

Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab concerning the verse, that he said: strength is the horse, up to the arrow and what is below it.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from ʿIkrimah, that he said: strength is fortresses, and ﴿of steeds of war﴾ is females.

al-Firyabi, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying: ﴿by which you will terrify the enemy of Allah and your enemy﴾, that he said: you will disgrace by it the enemy of Allah and your enemy.

Numerous hadiths have come concerning the recommendation of archery and the reward in it.

Likewise, hadiths have come concerning the recommendation of keeping horses and preparing them, and the great reward of their owner, which the scope of this discussion does not allow to be expanded upon.

A group of scholars have devoted separate works to this subject.

(p-548) **Al-junūḥ** (inclination) means *al-maydl* (leaning). One says *janaḥa al-rajulu ilā al-rajul*, meaning the man leaned toward the other man. From this comes the saying that the ribs are called *jawāniḥ* because they lean toward the inner organs (*al-ḥanwah*). *Janaḥat al-ibil* means the camels bent their necks while walking. From this is the verse of Dhū al-Rummah:

"When he dies atop the saddle, I revive his spirit with your remembrance, while the loosely led camels bow their necks (*junnaḥ*)."

A similar verse is that of ʿAntarah:

"Birds (*jawānīḥ*) that are certain their tribe, when the two hosts meet, will be the first to triumph."

He means birds. **Al-salm** means reconciliation (*al-ṣulḥ*).

Al-Aʿmash, Abū Bakr, Ibn Muḥayṣin and al-Mufaḍḍal read *al-silm* with a kasra on the sīn. The rest read it with a fatḥa.

Al-ʿUqaylī read *fa-jnuḥ* with a ḍamma on the nūn, and the rest read it with a fatḥa. The first is the dialect of Qays and the second is the dialect of Tamīm.

Ibn Jinnī said: the dialect of Qays is the analogical form, and *al-salm* is feminine just as *al-ḥarb* (war) is feminine. Or it is interpreted as *al-khaṣlah* (quality) or *al-fiʿlah* (act).

The scholars differed over whether this verse is abrogated (*manṣūkhah*, naskh) or unabrogated (*muḥkamah*). It was said that it is abrogated by His saying: ﴿So fight the polytheists﴾. It was also said that it is not abrogated, because what is meant by it is accepting the poll tax (*al-jizyah*), and the Companions and those after them accepted it from them. Therefore it is specific to the People of the Book. It was also said that if the polytheists call to reconciliation, it is permissible to respond to them. Those who prohibit reconciliation with the polytheists held to His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So do not weaken and call to peace while you are the superior, and Allah is with you﴾ (Muhammad: 35).

They restricted the impermissibility to when the Muslims are in a state of strength and power, not when they are not in that state. In that case it is permissible, as the Prophet (ﷺ) did when he made a truce with Quraysh. The caliphs and the Companions continued to act upon this. The discussion of the scholars on this question is well known and established in its proper places.

﴿And rely upon Allah﴾ in your inclination to peace, and do not fear their deception, for He, glory be to Him, is the All-Hearing of what they say, the All-Knowing of what they do.

﴿And if they intend to deceive you﴾ through the reconciliation, while they conceal treachery and deceit, ﴿then indeed Allah is sufficient for you﴾, that is, sufficient for you against what you fear of their evils through breaking the treaty and betrayal. The clause ﴿He it is who supported you with His help and with the believers﴾ is causal (*taʿlīliyyah*), meaning: do not fear their deceit and their scheming, for Allah, who strengthened you over them with victory in the past, namely on the day of Badr, is the One who will support you and strengthen you over them when deceit and treachery occur. By "the believers" are meant the Emigrants (*al-Muhājirūn*) and the Helpers (*al-Anṣār*).

Then He explained how His support through the believers occurred, saying: ﴿And He joined their hearts together﴾. Its apparent meaning is generality, and the harmony of the believers' hearts is among the causes of victory with which Allah supported His Messenger.

Most of the exegetes said: the intended meaning is the Aws and the Khazraj, for there was intense tribal fanaticism (*ʿaṣabiyyah*) among them and great wars, so Allah joined their hearts through faith in the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). It was also said that He intended the joining of the Emigrants and the Helpers. Taking it in its general sense is preferable, for before the Muhammadan mission (*al-biʿthah*) the Arabs would devour one another and did not respect one another's property or blood, until Islam came and they became one hand, and the tribal fanaticism that existed among them vanished. The clause ﴿Even if you had spent all that is in the earth, you could not have joined their hearts﴾ confirms the content of what precedes it.

The meaning is that the fanaticism and enmity that existed among them had reached a degree that could not be repelled under any circumstances. Even if the one seeking it had spent all that is in the earth, what he sought of joining would not have been achieved for him, because their matter in that regard had become extremely severe. ﴿But Allah joined them together﴾ by His great power and wondrous creation. Indeed He is the Mighty, whom no one can overcome, and no matter of affairs is beyond Him; the Wise in His management and in the effectiveness of His prohibition and command.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Mujāhid, regarding His saying ﴿And if they incline to peace﴾, that he said: "Qurayẓah."

Abū al-Shaykh transmitted from al-Suddī, regarding the verse, that he said: "It was revealed concerning the Banū Qurayẓah, and it was abrogated by ﴿So do not weaken and call to peace﴾ (Muhammad: 35) to the end of the verse."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "Al-salm is obedience."

Abū al-Shaykh transmitted from him regarding the verse, that he said: "If they are content, then be content."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Suddī regarding the verse, that he said: "If they desire reconciliation, then desire it."

Abū ʿUbayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding the verse, that he said: "It was abrogated by this verse: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah nor in the Last Day﴾ (al-Tawbah: 29) to His saying ﴿while they are humbled﴾ (al-Tawbah: 29)."

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Naḥḥās in his book on abrogation (*Nāsikhihi*), and Abū al-Shaykh transmitted from Qatādah, who said: "Then that was abrogated by ﴿So kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ (al-Tawbah: 5)."

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh transmitted from Mujāhid regarding His saying ﴿And if they intend to deceive you﴾ that he said: "Qurayẓah."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Suddī regarding His saying ﴿and with the believers﴾ that he said: "With the Helpers."

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr something similar.

Ibn Mardawayh also transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās something similar.

Ibn ʿAsākir transmitted from Abū Hurayrah, who said: "It is written upon the Throne: There is no god but Allah; I am Allah, alone, without partner. Muhammad is My servant and My messenger. I have supported him with My knowledge." That is His saying: ﴿He it is who supported you with His help and with the believers﴾.

Ibn al-Mubārak, Ibn Abī Shaybah, Ibn Abī al-Dunyā, al-Nasāʾī, al-Bazzār, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, Abū al-Shaykh, al-Ḥākim, who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqī in *al-Shuʿab*, transmitted from Ibn Masʿūd that this verse was revealed concerning those who love one another for the sake of Allah: ﴿Even if you had spent all that is in the earth﴾, the verse.

Abū ʿUbayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Abū al-Shaykh, and al-Bayhaqī in *Shuʿab al-Īmān* (the wording is his) transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "The ties of kinship are cut, the favour of the benefactor is denied, but we have not seen anything like the closeness of hearts. Allah says: ﴿Even if you had spent all that is in the earth﴾, the verse."

Ibn al-Mubārak, ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, Abū al-Shaykh, al-Ḥākim and al-Bayhaqī transmitted from him something similar. Nothing in what is transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās indicates that it is the occasion of revelation (*sabab al-nuzūl*). But the matter lies in the statement of Ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with him, that this verse was revealed concerning those who love one another for the sake of Allah. Yet the context before it is ﴿He it is who supported you with His help and with the believers﴾, and the context after it is ﴿O Prophet, Allah is sufficient for you and for those believers who follow you﴾ (al-Anfāl: 64). (p-549) Moreover, the pronoun in His saying ﴿you could not have joined their hearts﴾ refers without any doubt to the believers mentioned before it, and likewise the pronoun in His saying ﴿But Allah joined them together﴾. This indicates that the joining mentioned is among the believers whom Allah supported His Messenger (ﷺ) with.

Therefore it is specific to the People of the Book. It was also said that if the polytheists call to reconciliation, it is permissible to respond to them. Those who prohibit reconciliation with the polytheists held to His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So do not weaken and call to peace while you are the superior, and Allah is with you﴾ (Muhammad: 35).

They restricted the impermissibility to when the Muslims are in a state of strength and power, not when they are not in that state. In that case it is permissible, as the Prophet (ﷺ) did when he made a truce with Quraysh. The caliphs and the Companions continued to act upon this. The discussion of the scholars on this question is well known and established in its proper places.

﴿And rely upon Allah﴾ in your inclination to peace, and do not fear their deception, for He, glory be to Him, is the All-Hearing of what they say, the All-Knowing of what they do.

﴿And if they intend to deceive you﴾ through the reconciliation, while they conceal treachery and deceit, ﴿then indeed Allah is sufficient for you﴾, that is, sufficient for you against what you fear of their evils through breaking the treaty and betrayal. The clause ﴿He it is who supported you with His help and with the believers﴾ is causal (*taʿlīliyyah*), meaning: do not fear their deceit and their scheming, for Allah, who strengthened you over them with victory in the past, namely on the day of Badr, is the One who will support you and strengthen you over them when deceit and treachery occur. By "the believers" are meant the Emigrants (*al-Muhājirūn*) and the Helpers (*al-Anṣār*).

Then He explained how His support through the believers occurred, saying: ﴿And He joined their hearts together﴾. Its apparent meaning is generality, and the harmony of the believers' hearts is among the causes of victory with which Allah supported His Messenger.

Most of the exegetes said: the intended meaning is the Aws and the Khazraj, for there was intense tribal fanaticism (*ʿaṣabiyyah*) among them and great wars, so Allah joined their hearts through faith in the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). It was also said that He intended the joining of the Emigrants and the Helpers. Taking it in its general sense is preferable, for before the Muhammadan mission (*al-biʿthah*) the Arabs would devour one another and did not respect one another's property or blood, until Islam came and they became one hand, and the tribal fanaticism that existed among them vanished. The clause ﴿Even if you had spent all that is in the earth, you could not have joined their hearts﴾ confirms the content of what precedes it.

The meaning is that the fanaticism and enmity that existed among them had reached a degree that could not be repelled under any circumstances. Even if the one seeking it had spent all that is in the earth, what he sought of joining would not have been achieved for him, because their matter in that regard had become extremely severe. ﴿But Allah joined them together﴾ by His great power and wondrous creation. Indeed He is the Mighty, whom no one can overcome, and no matter of affairs is beyond Him; the Wise in His management and in the effectiveness of His prohibition and command.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Mujāhid, regarding His saying ﴿And if they incline to peace﴾, that he said: "Qurayẓah."

Abū al-Shaykh transmitted from al-Suddī, regarding the verse, that he said: "It was revealed concerning the Banū Qurayẓah, and it was abrogated by ﴿So do not weaken and call to peace﴾ (Muhammad: 35) to the end of the verse."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "Al-salm is obedience."

Abū al-Shaykh transmitted from him regarding the verse, that he said: "If they are content, then be content."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Suddī regarding the verse, that he said: "If they desire reconciliation, then desire it."

Abū ʿUbayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding the verse, that he said: "It was abrogated by this verse: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah nor in the Last Day﴾ (al-Tawbah: 29) to His saying ﴿while they are humbled﴾ (al-Tawbah: 29)."

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Naḥḥās in his book on abrogation (*Nāsikhihi*), and Abū al-Shaykh transmitted from Qatādah, who said: "Then that was abrogated by ﴿So kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ (al-Tawbah: 5)."

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh transmitted from Mujāhid regarding His saying ﴿And if they intend to deceive you﴾ that he said: "Qurayẓah."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Suddī regarding His saying ﴿and with the believers﴾ that he said: "With the Helpers."

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr something similar.

Ibn Mardawayh also transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās something similar.

Ibn ʿAsākir transmitted from Abū Hurayrah, who said: "It is written upon the Throne: There is no god but Allah; I am Allah, alone, without partner. Muhammad is My servant and My messenger. I have supported him with My knowledge." That is His saying: ﴿He it is who supported you with His help and with the believers﴾.

Ibn al-Mubārak, Ibn Abī Shaybah, Ibn Abī al-Dunyā, al-Nasāʾī, al-Bazzār, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, Abū al-Shaykh, al-Ḥākim, who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqī in *al-Shuʿab*, transmitted from Ibn Masʿūd that this verse was revealed concerning those who love one another for the sake of Allah: ﴿Even if you had spent all that is in the earth﴾, the verse.

Abū ʿUbayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Abū al-Shaykh, and al-Bayhaqī in *Shuʿab al-Īmān* (the wording is his) transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "The ties of kinship are cut, the favour of the benefactor is denied, but we have not seen anything like the closeness of hearts. Allah says: ﴿Even if you had spent all that is in the earth﴾, the verse."

Ibn al-Mubārak, ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, Abū al-Shaykh, al-Ḥākim and al-Bayhaqī transmitted from him something similar. Nothing in what is transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās indicates that it is the occasion of revelation (*sabab al-nuzūl*). But the matter lies in the statement of Ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with him, that this verse was revealed concerning those who love one another for the sake of Allah. Yet the context before it is ﴿He it is who supported you with His help and with the believers﴾, and the context after it is ﴿O Prophet, Allah is sufficient for you and for those believers who follow you﴾ (al-Anfāl: 64). (p-549) Moreover, the pronoun in His saying ﴿you could not have joined their hearts﴾ refers without any doubt to the believers mentioned before it, and likewise the pronoun in His saying ﴿But Allah joined them together﴾. This indicates that the joining mentioned is among the believers whom Allah supported His Messenger (ﷺ) with.

**Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 8, verses 64–66:**

His saying: ﴿O Prophet, God is sufficient for you and for those who follow you﴾ is not a repetition of what came before it, for the first (verse) is restricted to the intention of deception: ﴿And if they intend to deceive you, then God is sufficient for you﴾ (al-Anfal: 62). So that is a particular sufficiency, whereas in His saying ﴿O Prophet, God is sufficient for you﴾ there is a general, unrestricted sufficiency, meaning: God is sufficient for you in every circumstance.

The waw (and) in His saying ﴿and those who follow you﴾ may be a conjunction (ʿatf) upon the noble name (of the Prophet). The meaning would be: God is sufficient for you and the believers are sufficient for you, i.e., God is your protector and the believers are your protectors.

It may also be in the sense of "with" (maʿa), as you say: ḥasbuka wa-Zaydan dirham (the dirham is sufficient for you and Zayd), and the meaning would be: God is your sufficiency and the sufficiency of the believers, because conjoining a noun (ẓāhir) to a pronoun (muḍmar) in such a construction is impermissible, as is established in the science of grammar (naḥw). The Kufans permitted it.

Al-Farraʾ said: "It is not common in their speech to say ḥasbuka wa-akhīka (your sufficiency and your brother's). Rather, what is used is: ḥasbuka wa-ḥasbu akhīka, with the preposition repeated. So if His saying ﴿and those who follow you﴾ were in the genitive, it would have been said: God is sufficient for you and the sufficiency of those who follow you." Al-Naḥḥas preferred the accusative as the object of accompaniment (maf'ūl maʿahu).

It was also said: the meaning may be: "And those who follow you among the believers, God is sufficient for them," so the predicate has been omitted.

His saying: ﴿Urge the believers to fighting﴾, i.e., incite them and spur them on. Al-taḥrīḍ (incitement) linguistically means exaggeration in urging, and it is similar to al-taḥḍīḍ (urging). It is derived from al-ḥaraḍ (ruin), which is when illness wears a person down and intensifies until he is near death, as if (the one who urges) attributes to him destruction if he lags behind what he has been commanded. Then (God) gave them good news, to firm up their hearts and calm their thoughts, that the steadfast among them in fighting would overcome ten times their number of unbelievers. So He said: ﴿If there are twenty steadfast among you, they will overcome two hundred﴾. Then He added this for clarification, indicating that this glad tidings is not restricted to this number, but applies to every number, so He said: ﴿And if there are a hundred of you, they will overcome a thousand﴾. In this is an indication that a group of believers, whether few or many, will by no means be overcome by ten times their number of unbelievers. Yet something in external reality contradicts this: how many groups of the unbelievers have overcome someone a tenth of their number of Muslims, or even half of them, or equal to them?

It is answered that the existence of this in external reality does not contradict what is in the verse, because it is possible that the group of believers were not characterized by the quality of steadfastness. It was also said: this statement in the verse has the meaning of a command, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And mothers suckle (their children)﴾ (al-Baqarah: 233) and ﴿And divorced women wait (by themselves)﴾ (al-Baqarah: 228). So the believers were commanded by God, glory be to Him, that a group of them should stand firm against ten times their number. Then, when that was hard for them and they found it great, He lightened it for them and granted them a concession, because He, glory be to Him, knew the weakness that was among them. So He said: ﴿Now, if there are among you a hundred steadfast, they will overcome two hundred﴾ to the end of the verse, so He made it obligatory for one (believer) to stand firm against two of the unbelievers.

Hamzah, on the authority of ʿĀṣim, read ḍaʿfan (weakness) with a fatḥah on the ḍād.

His saying: ﴿because they are a people who do not understand﴾ is connected to His saying ﴿they will overcome﴾, i.e., this overcoming is due to their ignorance and lack of understanding, and that they fight without insight. Whoever is like this is, for the most part, overcome.

It has been said, regarding the point of specifying that twenty overcome two hundred and a hundred overcome a thousand: his expeditions (sarāyā) which he (ﷺ) sent out never numbered fewer than twenty nor more than a hundred. It was also said: the specifying of what comes after that, namely that a hundred overcome two hundred and a thousand overcome two thousand, is a glad tiding to the Muslims that the armies of Islam will one day exceed tens and hundreds, reaching thousands.

Then He informed them that this overcoming is by the permission of God, His facilitation and ease, not by their strength and endurance. Then He gave them good news that He is with the steadfast. In this is encouragement to patience, emphasis upon adhering to it, and recommendation of it, and that it is among the greatest causes of success, triumph, victory and prevailing, because whoever God is with, no one can overcome him.

The people of knowledge have differed over whether this lightening is abrogation (naskh, the cancellation of a earlier ruling by a later one) or not, and there is no great benefit tied to that.

Al-Bazzar related, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: When ʿUmar embraced Islam, the polytheists said: "Today the people have gained the upper hand over us." And God revealed: ﴿O Prophet, God is sufficient for you and for those who follow you among the believers﴾.

Al-Ṭabarānī, Abū al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh related, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "When thirty-nine men and a woman had embraced Islam with the Prophet (ﷺ), then ʿUmar embraced Islam, and they became forty, and (the verse) was revealed: ﴿O Prophet, God is sufficient for you and for those who follow you among the believers﴾."

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh related, on the authority of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: "When thirty-three men and six women had embraced Islam with the Prophet (ﷺ), then ʿUmar embraced Islam, (the verse) ﴿O Prophet, God is sufficient for you﴾ was revealed."

Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Abi Hatim related, on the authority of al-Zuhri, regarding the verse, that he said: It was revealed concerning the Ansar.

Al-Bukhari in his History, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abū al-Shaykh related, on the authority of al-Shaʿbi, regarding His saying: ﴿O Prophet, God is sufficient for you and for those who follow you among the believers﴾, that he said: "God is sufficient for you and the sufficiency of those who follow you."

Al-Bukhari, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abū al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in Shuʿab al-Iman related, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: When the verse ﴿If there are among you twenty steadfast, they will overcome two hundred﴾ was revealed, it was prescribed for them that not one of them should flee from ten. Then the verse ﴿Now God has lightened your burden﴾ was revealed, to the end of the verse, and it was prescribed that a hundred should not flee from two hundred. Sufyan said, and Ibn Shubrumah said: "I consider enjoining good and forbidding evil to be like this: if they are two men, he should command them, and if they are three, he is free from leaving them (i.e., he has latitude)."

Al-Bukhari, al-Nahhas in his Nasikh (Book of Abrogation), Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan related, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: When the verse ﴿If there are among you twenty steadfast, they will overcome two hundred﴾ was revealed, it was hard for the Muslims, when it was prescribed for them that not one should flee from ten. Then the relief came: ﴿Now God has lightened your burden﴾, to the end of the verse. He said: "So when God lightened the number for them, the steadfastness decreased by the same amount as He lightened for them."

(p-٥٥٠)

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh related, on the authority of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: "When thirty-three men and six women had embraced Islam with the Prophet (ﷺ), then ʿUmar embraced Islam, (the verse) ﴿O Prophet, God is sufficient for you﴾ was revealed."

Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Abi Hatim related, on the authority of al-Zuhri, regarding the verse, that he said: It was revealed concerning the Ansar.

Al-Bukhari in his History, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abū al-Shaykh related, on the authority of al-Shaʿbi, regarding His saying: ﴿O Prophet, God is sufficient for you and for those who follow you among the believers﴾, that he said: "God is sufficient for you and the sufficiency of those who follow you."

Sufyan said, and Ibn Shubrumah said: "I consider enjoining good and forbidding evil to be like this: if they are two men, he should command them, and if they are three, he is free from leaving them (i.e., he has latitude)."

(p-٥٥٠)

This is another ruling concerning jihad.

The meaning of ﴿It is not for a Prophet﴾ is: it is not valid for him and does not befit him. The word is derived from al-asr, which means a leather thong, because they used to bind the prisoner with it. Thus anyone taken captive is called asir, even if he was not bound with leather. Al-A'sha said:

"Poetry shackled me in its house, as the thongs bind the donkey."

Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' said: al-Asra are those who are not bound when they are captured, while al-Usara are those who are bound in slavery.

Al-ithkhan (intensive subduing) means the great abundance of killing and going to extremes in it. The Arabs say: "Fulan athkhana fi hadha al-amr," meaning he went to extremes in this matter.

So the meaning is: it is not for a Prophet to have prisoners until he has gone to extremes in slaying the disbelievers and has increased it. It is also said that the meaning of al-ithkhan is firm establishment, and it is also said that it means strength.

Allah, glory be to Him, informed that killing the polytheists on the day of Badr was more preferable than taking them captive and ransoming them. Then, when the Muslims increased in number, Allah granted leave for that, saying: ﴿Then either grace afterwards or ransom﴾ (Muhammad 4), as will come in Surat al-Qital, Allah willing.

His saying: ﴿You desire the goods of this worldly life﴾ means its benefit and its enjoyment, by what you have taken of ransom. It was called "'arad" (goods) because it swiftly passes away, just as accidents (a'rad), which are the opposite of substances, pass away. ﴿But Allah desires the Hereafter﴾ means He desires for you the Abode of the Hereafter, through the reward you gain by intensive killing.

It was also read "yuridu al-akhirata" with the genitive (jarr), on the assumption of an omitted noun, which is the one mentioned before it: that is, "and Allah desires the goods of the Hereafter." ﴿And Allah is Mighty﴾, not overcome, ﴿Wise﴾ in all His actions.

His saying: ﴿Had it not been for a decree from Allah that preceded, a great punishment would have touched you for what you took.﴾

The exegetes differed about what this preceding decree was. There are several views:

The first: what had preceded in Allah's knowledge, that He would make the spoils lawful for this nation after they had been forbidden to the other nations.

The second: that it is Allah's forgiveness of the people of Badr for what they had done before and after, as in the authentic hadith: "Allah looked upon the people of Badr and said, 'Do what you wish, for I have forgiven you.'"

The third view: that He would not punish them while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was among them, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And Allah would not punish them while you are among them﴾ (al-Anfal 33).

The fourth view: that He does not punish anyone for a sin committed in ignorance of its being a sin.

The fifth view: that it is what Allah decreed of erasing minor sins through avoiding major sins.

The sixth view: that He does not punish anyone except after the proof has been firmly established and the prohibition has been sent ahead, and no prohibition had preceded concerning that.

Ibn Jarir al-Tabari held that all these meanings are included under the wording and that it encompasses them all. ﴿Would have touched you﴾ means would have befallen you. ﴿For what you took﴾ means on account of what you took of ransom. ﴿A great punishment﴾.

The fa' in ﴿So eat of what you have gained﴾ indicates the sequence of what follows upon an omitted cause. That is: "I have made the spoils lawful for you, so eat of what you have gained." It may also be a conjunction upon an omitted supposition: "Leave the ransom, so eat of what you have gained apart from it." It was also said that "ma" refers to the ransom: "Eat of the ransom that you have gained, for it is part of the spoils that Allah has made lawful for you." ﴿Lawful and good﴾ are in the accusative as a state (hal) or as an attribute of an omitted verbal noun: that is, "eating lawfully and good." ﴿And fear Allah﴾ regarding what is to come, so do not proceed to anything that Allah has not permitted you. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving﴾ of what has passed from you, ﴿Merciful﴾ to you. Therefore He granted you leave to accept ransom in the future.

Ahmad reported from Anas, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) consulted the people about the prisoners on the day of Badr, saying: 'Indeed Allah has granted you power over them.' Then Umar ibn al-Khattab stood up and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, strike their necks!' The Prophet (ﷺ) turned away from him. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came back and said: 'O people, indeed Allah has granted you power over them, and they are only your brothers of yesterday.' Umar stood up and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, strike their necks!' The Prophet (ﷺ) turned away from him, then came back and said the same. Then Abu Bakr al-Siddiq stood up and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we think that you should pardon them and accept ransom from them.' So he pardoned them and accepted ransom from them. Abdullah ibn Rawaha said: 'O Messenger of Allah, look for a valley full of firewood and set it alight upon them.' Al-Abbas, who was listening, said: 'You have severed your ties of kinship!' The exegetes differed about what this preceding decree was. There are several views:

The first: what had preceded in Allah's knowledge, that He would make the spoils lawful for this nation after they had been forbidden to the other nations.

The second: that it is Allah's forgiveness of the people of Badr for what they had done before and after, as in the authentic hadith: "Allah looked upon the people of Badr and said, 'Do what you wish, for I have forgiven you.'"

The third view: that He would not punish them while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was among them, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And Allah would not punish them while you are among them﴾ (al-Anfal 33).

The fourth view: that He does not punish anyone for a sin committed in ignorance of its being a sin.

The fifth view: that it is what Allah decreed of erasing minor sins through avoiding major sins.

The sixth view: that He does not punish anyone except after the proof has been firmly established and the prohibition has been sent ahead, and no prohibition had preceded concerning that.

Ibn Jarir al-Tabari held that all these meanings are included under the wording and that it encompasses them all. ﴿Would have touched you﴾ means would have befallen you. ﴿For what you took﴾ means on account of what you took of ransom. ﴿A great punishment﴾.

The fa' in ﴿So eat of what you have gained﴾ indicates the sequence of what follows upon an omitted cause. That is: "I have made the spoils lawful for you, so eat of what you have gained." It may also be a conjunction upon an omitted supposition: "Leave the ransom, so eat of what you have gained apart from it." It was also said that "ma" refers to the ransom: "Eat of the ransom that you have gained, for it is part of the spoils that Allah has made lawful for you." ﴿Lawful and good﴾ are in the accusative as a state (hal) or as an attribute of an omitted verbal noun: that is, "eating lawfully and good." ﴿And fear Allah﴾ regarding what is to come, so do not proceed to anything that Allah has not permitted you. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving﴾ of what has passed from you, ﴿Merciful﴾ to you. Therefore He granted you leave to accept ransom in the future.

Ahmad reported from Anas, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) consulted the people about the prisoners on the day of Badr, saying: 'Indeed Allah has granted you power over them.' Then Umar ibn al-Khattab stood up and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, strike their necks!' The Prophet (ﷺ) turned away from him. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came back and said: 'O people, indeed Allah has granted you power over them, and they are only your brothers of yesterday.' Umar stood up and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, strike their necks!' The Prophet (ﷺ) turned away from him, then came back and said the same. Then Abu Bakr al-Siddiq stood up and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we think that you should pardon them and accept ransom from them.' So he pardoned them and accepted ransom from them. Then Allah revealed: ﴿Had it not been for a decree from Allah that preceded﴾, the verse."

Ibn Abi Shayba, Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi (who graded it hasan), Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim (who graded it sahih), Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il reported from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "On the day of Badr the prisoners were brought, and among them was al-Abbas. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'What do you think of these prisoners?' Abu Bakr said: 'O Messenger of Allah, they are your people and your family. Spare them, perhaps Allah will turn to them in forgiveness.' Umar said: 'O Messenger of Allah, they denied you, drove you out and fought you. Bring them forward and strike their necks.' Abdullah ibn Rawaha said: 'O Messenger of Allah, look for a valley full of firewood and set it alight upon them.' Al-Abbas, who was listening, said: 'You have severed your ties of kinship!' The Prophet (ﷺ) entered upon them and did not answer them with anything. Some people said: 'He will take the view of Abu Bakr.' Others said: 'He will take the view of Umar.' Others said: 'He will take the view of Abdullah ibn Rawaha.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out and said: 'Indeed Allah softens the hearts of some men until they are softer than milk, and Allah hardens the hearts of some men until they are harder than stones. Your likeness, O Abu Bakr, is the likeness of Abraham (peace be upon him), who said: ﴿Whoever follows me is of me, and whoever disobeys me, indeed You are Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (Ibrahim 36). Your likeness, O Abu Bakr, is the likeness of Jesus (peace be upon him), who said: ﴿If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants, and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Mighty, the Wise﴾ (al-Ma'idah 118). Your likeness, O Umar, is the likeness of Noah (peace be upon him), who said: ﴿My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers a dweller﴾ (Nuh 26). Your likeness, O Umar, is the likeness of Moses (peace be upon him), who said: ﴿Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment﴾ (Yunus 88). You are poor, so let none of them escape except with ransom or the striking of a neck." Abdullah said: "O Messenger of Allah, except Suhayl ibn Bayda', for I heard him mention Islam." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fell silent. "I have never been in a day more afraid that stones would fall upon me from the sky than that day, until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Except Suhayl ibn Bayda'.'" Then Allah revealed: ﴿It is not for a Prophet to have prisoners﴾, the verse.

Al-Hakim (who graded it sahih), Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan reported from Ali, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) said concerning the prisoners of Badr: 'If you wish, you may kill them, and if you wish, you may ransom them and benefit from the ransom, and from you there will be a martyr equal to their number.' The last of the seventy to be martyred was Thabit ibn Qays, who was martyred at al-Yamama."

Abd al-Razzaq in his Musannaf and Ibn Abi Shayba reported similarly from Ubayda.

Al-Hakim (who graded it sahih) and Ibn Mardawayh reported from Ibn Umar, who said: "When the prisoners of Badr were taken, al-Abbas was taken among those captured. A man from the Ansar captured him, and the Ansar had promised to kill him. This reached the Prophet (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'I did not sleep last night because of my uncle al-Abbas, and the Ansar claim that they will kill him.' Umar said to him: 'Shall I go to them?' He said: 'Yes.' Umar went to the Ansar and said: 'Release al-Abbas.' They said: 'No, by Allah, we will not release him.' Umar said to them: 'If the Messenger of Allah is pleased?' They said: 'If the Messenger of Allah is pleased, then take him.' Umar took him, and when he was in his hand he said: 'O Abbas, embrace Islam, for by Allah, your embracing Islam is dearer to me than that al-Khattab should embrace Islam, and I say this only because I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) delighted by your Islam.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) consulted Abu Bakr, and Abu Bakr said: 'Your kinsmen, so release them.' He consulted Umar, and Umar said: 'Kill them.' So the Messenger of Allah ransomed them, and Allah revealed: ﴿It is not for a Prophet to have prisoners﴾, the verse."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh reported from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿until he has subdued in the land﴾, that it means until they gain dominance over the land.

Ibn Abi Shayba, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn al-Mundhir reported from Mujahid, who said: "al-Ithkhan is killing."

Ibn Abi Shayba and Ibn al-Mundhir reported from Mujahid also, regarding the verse, who said: "Then the concession was revealed afterwards: if you wish, show grace, and if you wish, ransom."

Ibn al-Mundhir reported from Qatada, regarding ﴿You desire the goods of the worldly life﴾, who said: "The companions of Muhammad (ﷺ) desired ransom on the day of Badr, so they ransomed them for four thousand each, four thousand each."

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ikrima, regarding ﴿You desire the goods of the worldly life﴾, who said: "It is the kharaj (tribute)."

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿Had it not been for a decree from Allah that preceded﴾, who said: "It preceded for them with forgiveness."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh reported from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "It is what preceded for the people of Badr of happiness."

Al-Nasa'i, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu al-Shaykh reported from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Mercy from Allah preceded for them before they committed disobedience."

Abu Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh reported from Mujahid, who said: "It preceded that He would not punish anyone until He had made it clear to him and sent warning to him."

Disagreement among the readers (qurra') concerning "asra" and "al-usara" here is as it was in the verse before this one. God addressed His Prophet ﷺ with this: that is, say to these captives who are in your hands, whom you took captive on the Day of Badr and from whom you took ransom: ﴿If God knows in your hearts any good﴾ from sound faith, righteous intention, and sincerity of disposition, ﴿He will give you better than what was taken from you﴾ of ransom: that is, He will compensate you in this world with provision better than it and more beneficial to you, or in the Hereafter with the reward He records for you for righteous deeds. ﴿And He will forgive you﴾ your sins. ﴿And God is Forgiving, Merciful﴾; it is His nature to forgive His servants and to show mercy to them.

When He had mentioned the compensation for those in whose hearts He knows good, He mentioned those who are opposite to that among them, saying: ﴿But if they intend treachery against you﴾ by what they have said to you with their tongues, that they have believed in you and affirmed you, while that did not come from them out of a true resolve and sincere intention, but is rather deception and trickery. So it is not unlikely from them, for they have already done something greater than it, namely that they betrayed God before you gained mastery over them, so they disbelieved in Him and fought His Messenger. ﴿So He enabled [you] against them﴾ by giving you victory over them on the Day of Badr, so you killed whom you killed of them and took captive whom you took captive. ﴿And God is Knowing﴾ of what is in their inner selves, ﴿Wise﴾ in His actions toward them.

Al-Hakim, who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan, related from 'Aishah, who said: "When the people of Makkah sent [payments] for the ransom of their captives, Zaynab, the daughter of the Messenger of God ﷺ, sent [a ransom] for Abu al-'As and sent with it a necklace. When the Messenger of God ﷺ saw it, he was moved with direct tenderness and said: 'If you see fit, release her captive for her.' Al-'Abbas said: 'I was a Muslim, O Messenger of God.' He said: 'God knows your Islam; if you are as you say, then God will reward you. Ransom yourself, and your two nephews Nawfal ibn al-Harith and 'Aqil ibn Abi Talib, and your ally 'Utbah ibn 'Amr.' He said: 'That is not with me, O Messenger of God.' He said: 'Then where is the wealth which you and Umm al-Fadl buried? You said to her: If I am killed, this wealth is for my sons.' He said: 'By God, O Messenger of God, this is something no one knew but me and her.' [He said:] 'Then reckon for me what you have taken from me: twenty ounces of wealth which was with me.' He said: 'I will not do that.' So he ransomed himself, his two nephews, and his ally, and the verse was revealed: ﴿Say to those in your hands of the captives...﴾ to the end of the verse. In exchange for the twenty ounces, God gave me in Islam twenty slaves, each of whom has wealth with which he trades, along with what I hope for of God's forgiveness."

Ibn Sa'd, and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, related from Abu Musa: "That al-'Ala' ibn al-Hadrami sent to the Messenger of God (p-552) ﷺ wealth from Bahrain amounting to eighty thousand, and no wealth had ever come to the Messenger of God ﷺ that was greater than it. It was spread out on a mat, and the people came, and the Messenger of God ﷺ began giving to them, and on that day there was no counting or weighing. Then al-'Abbas came and said: 'O Messenger of God, I gave my own ransom and the ransom of 'Aqil on the Day of Badr; give me from this wealth.' He said: 'Take.' So he scooped it into his garment, then went to leave but could not manage it. He raised his head and said: 'O Messenger of God, lift it onto me.' The Messenger of God ﷺ smiled and went away saying: 'As for one of the two things God promised, He has fulfilled it for us, and we do not know what He will do with the other.' ﴿Say to those in your hands of the captives: if God knows any good in your hearts, He will give you better than what was taken from you and will forgive you.﴾" So this is better than what was taken from me, and I do not know what will be done about forgiveness."

The narrations on this subject are numerous.

Ibn Sa'd and Ibn 'Asakir related from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding the verse, that he said: "It was revealed concerning the captives on the Day of Badr, among them al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, Nawfal ibn al-Harith, and 'Aqil ibn Abi Talib."

Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh related from him, regarding His saying: ﴿But if they intend treachery against you﴾, that if their statement was false ﴿then they have already betrayed God before, so He enabled [you] against them﴾: they disbelieved and fought you, so God enabled you over them.
