**Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on Surah 8, verses 72–75**

God, glorified is He, concluded this surah by mentioning *al-muwalah* (loyal allegiance), so that every group would know the one whose support it seeks. He, glorified is He, named those who migrated to Medina by this name (*al-Muhajirun*, the Emigrants), because they abandoned their homelands and left them seeking what is with God and responding to His caller. ﴿Those who gave refuge and gave help﴾ are the Ansar (the Helpers). The demonstrative in His words "Those" refers to the first and last relative pronouns. It is a subject (*mubtada'*), and its predicate (*khabar*) is the sentence mentioned after it. It is also permissible for "some of them" to be an apposition (*badal*) to the demonstrative. The predicate is ﴿allies of one another﴾, meaning that some of them are allies of others in support and assistance. It has also been said that the meaning is that some of them are allies of others in inheritance.

They used to inherit from one another on the basis of emigration and support. Then this was abrogated (*nusikha*, i.e. superseded by a later ruling) by His words, glorified is He: ﴿But those related by blood are closer to one another﴾.

His words ﴿And those who believed﴾ are the subject, and its predicate is ﴿you have no duty of guardianship toward them at all﴾.

Yahya ibn Wthab, al-A'mash and Hamzah read *min wilayatihim* with a kasra on the waw.

The rest read it with a fatha on it, meaning: you have no share of their support and assistance, or of their inheritance, even if they were among your relatives, because they had not emigrated. ﴿Until they emigrate﴾, so that they would have what the first group had, those who combined faith and emigration. ﴿And if they seek your help﴾, meaning these who believed but did not emigrate, if they ask you for help against the polytheists ﴿then it is incumbent upon you to help﴾, meaning it is obligatory upon you to help, except when they seek your help ﴿against a people with whom you have a treaty﴾. Then you should not help them, and you should not break the covenant between you and those people until its term expires.

Al-Zajjaj said: it is also permissible to read *fa-'alaykumu al-nasra* with the accusative, as an incitement (*al-igra'*).

His words ﴿And those who disbelieved﴾ are the subject, and its predicate is ﴿some of them are allies of others﴾, meaning some of them support others and take charge of their affairs, or inherit from one another when one dies. In this there is an implicit reproach to the Muslims, that they do not support the disbelievers or take them as allies.

His words ﴿If you do not do it﴾: the pronoun refers to what they were commanded before this, namely allegiance to the believers and supporting them in the detailed manner mentioned, and abandoning allegiance to the disbelievers. ﴿There will be turmoil on earth﴾, meaning turmoil will occur if you do not do that. ﴿And great corruption﴾, meaning a great harm in religion and in the world.

Then He, glorified is He, clarified another ruling relating to the believing emigrants who strove in the way of God, and the believers who gave refuge to those who emigrated to them and helped them, namely the Ansar. So He said: ﴿Those are the believers truly﴾, meaning those who are perfect in faith. This is not a repetition of what came before, for the earlier verse concerns the making of allegiance and support obligatory, while this verse is in praise of these people. Then He, glorified is He, informed that for them there is forgiveness of their sins in the Hereafter, and for them in this world there is ﴿generous provision﴾, pure, free of turbidity, good and pleasant.

Then He, glorified is He, informed that whoever emigrated after them and strove alongside the first strivers and the Ansar is one of them, meaning one of the first Emigrants and the Ansar in deserving what they deserved of allegiance and support, perfection of faith, forgiveness and generous provision.

Then He, glorified is He, clarified that ﴿those related by blood are closer to one another﴾ than others who are not related by kinship, in regard to inheritance. The intended meaning of "those related by blood" is kinsfolk, so it includes every relative. It has been said that what is meant here is the *'asabah* (agnatic heirs, male relatives through the father's line). They said: from this is the saying of the Arabs, "A kinship tie has joined you," for they do not mean kinship through the mother.

They said: from this is the verse of Qutaylah:

*The swords of his father's sons kept tearing at him,*
*By God, there are ties of kinship there being torn apart.*

It is not hidden from you that there is nothing in this which prevents its application to other than the agnatic heirs. The verse has been used as evidence by those who affirm the inheritance of *dhawu al-arham* (distant kin, relatives who are neither sharers nor agnatic heirs) according to the technical terminology of the scholars of inheritance (*'ilm al-mawarith*). The disagreement on this is well known and established in its proper place.

It has been said that this verse abrogates inheritance by allegiance and support, according to those who interpret the earlier words ﴿some of them are allies of others﴾ and what follows as referring to inheritance. As for those who interpret it as referring to support and assistance, they make this verse an announcement from Him, glorified and exalted is He, that kinsfolk ﴿are closer to one another in the Book of God﴾, meaning in His ruling, or in the Preserved Tablet (*al-Lawh al-Mahfuz*), or in the Qur'an. Inheritance enters this priority first, because its cause, namely kinship, exists. ﴿Indeed God is Knowing of all things﴾, nothing is hidden from Him of things, whatever they may be, and among that is what these verses contain.

(p. 553) Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿Indeed those who believed and emigrated﴾ to the end of the verse, that he said: the believers during the time of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) were in three states. Among them was the believer who emigrated and separated from his people. Regarding His words ﴿And those who gave refuge and gave help﴾ he said: they gave refuge, gave help, and proclaimed what the people of emigration proclaimed, and they drew swords against those who denied and rejected. These two are believers whom God made allies of one another. Regarding His words ﴿And those who believed but did not emigrate﴾ he said: they used to inherit among themselves when a believing emigrant died, through the guardianship in religion. The one who believed but did not emigrate did not inherit, because he had not emigrated and had not given help. So God absolved the believing emigrants from inheriting from them, and this is the guardianship about which He said: ﴿You have no duty of guardianship toward them at all until they emigrate. And if they seek your help in religion, then it is incumbent upon you to help, except against a people with whom you have a treaty﴾. It was binding upon the believers who gave refuge and gave help, when they sought their help in religion, that they should help them if they were fought against, except if they sought help against a people with whom they and the Prophet (ﷺ) had a covenant. Then there is no help for them against those people except against an enemy with whom they have no covenant. Then God revealed after that: join every kinsman to his kin among the believers who believed. ﴿And those who believed but did not emigrate﴾, so He gave every person among the believers a prescribed share, by His words: ﴿But those related by blood are closer to one another﴾ to the end of the verse.

In a narration of Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿Those are allies of one another﴾, he said: meaning in inheritance. God made the inheritance for the Emigrants and the Ansar, to the exclusion of the kin. ﴿And those who believed but did not emigrate, you have no duty of guardianship toward them at all﴾, meaning you have no share of their inheritance at all, ﴿until they emigrate. And if they seek your help in religion﴾, meaning if the Muslim bedouins seek help from the Emigrants and the Ansar against an enemy of theirs, then they are obliged to help them, except against a people with whom you have a treaty. They continued to act accordingly until God revealed this verse: ﴿But those related by blood are closer to one another﴾, so it abrogated the verse before it, and inheritance became for the kin.

Abu 'Ubayd, Abu Dawud, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him also, regarding these verses, that he said: the emigrant would not take a bedouin as his ally, nor would he inherit from him even if he was a believer, and the bedouin would not inherit from the emigrant. This verse abrogated that: ﴿But those related by blood are closer to one another in the Book of God﴾.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him also that he said: a man from among the Muslims said: "We shall make our near kin among the polytheists inherit from us." So this was revealed: ﴿And those who disbelieved, some of them are allies of others. If you do not do it, there will be turmoil on earth and great corruption﴾.

Ahmad, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, narrated from Jarir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The emigrants are allies of one another in this world and the Hereafter, and the freed captives (*al-tulaqa'*) of Quraysh and the manumitted slaves (*al-'utaqa'*) of Thaqif are allies of one another in this world and the Hereafter."

Al-Hakim, who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Usamah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The people of two religions do not inherit from one another. A Muslim does not inherit from a disbeliever, nor a disbeliever from a Muslim." Then he recited: ﴿And those who disbelieved, some of them are allies of others﴾ to the end of the verse.

Ibn Sa'd, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam, who said: God revealed about us specifically, the company of Quraysh: ﴿And those related by blood are closer to one another in the Book of God﴾. That was because we, the company of Quraysh, when we came to Medina, we came with no wealth. We found the Ansar excellent brothers, so we became brothers with them, and they made us their heirs, and we made them our heirs. Abu Bakr became brother to Kharijah ibn Zayd, 'Umar became brother to a certain man, and 'Uthman ibn 'Affan became brother to a man from the Banu Zurayq ibn As'ad al-Zurqi. (p. 553) Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿Indeed those who believed and emigrated﴾ to the end of the verse, that he said: the believers during the time of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) were in three states. Among them was the believer who emigrated and separated from his people. Regarding His words ﴿And those who gave refuge and gave help﴾ he said: they gave refuge, gave help, and proclaimed what the people of emigration proclaimed, and they drew swords against those who denied and rejected. These two are believers whom God made allies of one another. Regarding His words ﴿And those who believed but did not emigrate﴾ he said: they used to inherit among themselves when a believing emigrant died, through the guardianship in religion. The one who believed but did not emigrate did not inherit, because he had not emigrated and had not given help. So God absolved the believing emigrants from inheriting from them, and this is the guardianship about which He said: ﴿You have no duty of guardianship toward them at all until they emigrate. And if they seek your help in religion, then it is incumbent upon you to help, except against a people with whom you have a treaty﴾. It was binding upon the believers who gave refuge and gave help, when they sought their help in religion, that they should help them if they were fought against, except if they sought help against a people with whom they and the Prophet (ﷺ) had a covenant. Then there is no help for them against those people except against an enemy with whom they have no covenant. Then God revealed after that: join every kinsman to his kin among the believers who believed. ﴿And those who believed but did not emigrate﴾, so He gave every person among the believers a prescribed share, by His words: ﴿But those related by blood are closer to one another﴾ to the end of the verse.

In a narration of Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿Those are allies of one another﴾, he said: meaning in inheritance. God made the inheritance for the Emigrants and the Ansar, to the exclusion of the kin. ﴿And those who believed but did not emigrate, you have no duty of guardianship toward them at all﴾, meaning you have no share of their inheritance at all, ﴿until they emigrate. And if they seek your help in religion﴾, meaning if the Muslim bedouins seek help from the Emigrants and the Ansar against an enemy of theirs, then they are obliged to help them, except against a people with whom you have a treaty. They continued to act accordingly until God revealed this verse: ﴿But those related by blood are closer to one another﴾, so it abrogated the verse before it, and inheritance became for the kin.

Abu 'Ubayd, Abu Dawud, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him also, regarding these verses, that he said: the emigrant would not take a bedouin as his ally, nor would he inherit from him even if he was a believer, and the bedouin would not inherit from the emigrant. This verse abrogated that: ﴿But those related by blood are closer to one another in the Book of God﴾.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him also that he said: a man from among the Muslims said: "We shall make our near kin among the polytheists inherit from us." So this was revealed: ﴿And those who disbelieved, some of them are allies of others. If you do not do it, there will be turmoil on earth and great corruption﴾.

Ahmad, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, narrated from Jarir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The emigrants are allies of one another in this world and the Hereafter, and the freed captives (*al-tulaqa'*) of Quraysh and the manumitted slaves (*al-'utaqa'*) of Thaqif are allies of one another in this world and the Hereafter."

Al-Hakim, who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Usamah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The people of two religions do not inherit from one another. A Muslim does not inherit from a disbeliever, nor a disbeliever from a Muslim." Then he recited: ﴿And those who disbelieved, some of them are allies of others﴾ to the end of the verse.

Ibn Sa'd, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam, who said: God revealed about us specifically, the company of Quraysh: ﴿And those related by blood are closer to one another in the Book of God﴾. That was because we, the company of Quraysh, when we came to Medina, we came with no wealth. We found the Ansar excellent brothers, so we became brothers with them, and they made us their heirs, and we made them our heirs. Abu Bakr became brother to Kharijah ibn Zayd, 'Umar became brother to a certain man, and 'Uthman ibn 'Affan became brother to a man from the Banu Zurayq ibn As'ad al-Zurqi. Al-Zubayr said: I became brother to Ka'b ibn Malik, and they inherited from us and we inherited from them. When the day of Uhud came, it was said to me: "Your brother Ka'b ibn Malik has been killed." So I went to him and turned him over, and I found that the weapons had weighed him down, as it seemed. By God, my son, if he had died that day, none would have inherited him except me. Then God revealed this verse about us, the company of Quraysh and the Ansar, and we returned to our inheritances.

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) made brotherhood among his companions, and some of them inherited from others, until this verse was revealed: ﴿But those related by blood are closer to one another﴾. So they abandoned that and inherited by lineage."
